translations.idiomatic: The biographies continue with Li Zhen and Wang Xin.

translations.idiomatic: Peng Lun, Ou Pan, and Zhang You

sentences.zh: 韓觀，字彥賓，虹人，高陽忠壯侯成子也。

translations.literal: Han Guan, styled Yanbin, was a man of Hong, son of Han Cheng, Marquis of Gaoyang with the posthumous epithet Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guan, courtesy name Yanbin, came from Hong. He was the son of Han Cheng, Marquis of Gaoyang, posthumously honored as Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 以舍人宿衛，忠謹為太祖所知，授桂林右衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: As an attendant he served in the palace guard; his loyalty and prudence won the founding emperor's notice, and he was appointed vice commander of the Guilin Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a palace attendant on night duty, he impressed the founding emperor with his loyalty and discretion and was appointed vice commander of the Guilin Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武十九年討平柳州、融縣諸蠻，累遷廣西都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu he campaigned against and pacified the various tribes of Liuzhou and Rong county, and was promoted in stages to regional military commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 19 he suppressed the tribal uprisings in Liuzhou and Rong county and rose through successive promotions to become military commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年平富川蠻，設靈亭千戶所。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he pacified the tribes of Fuchuan and established the Lingting thousand-household office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he pacified the Fuchuan tribes and established the Lingting thousand-household garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十五年平賓州上林蠻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he pacified the tribes of Shanglin in Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he pacified the Shanglin tribes in Bin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十七年會湖廣兵討全州、灌陽諸瑤，斬千四百余人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he joined Huguang forces to campaign against the Yao of Quanzhou, Guanyang, and other places, beheading more than fourteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he combined with Huguang troops to campaign against the Yao of Quanzhou and Guanyang, killing more than 1,400.

sentences.zh: 明年捕擒宜山諸縣蠻，斬其偽王及萬戶以下二千八百余人。

translations.literal: The next year he captured the tribes of Yishan and other counties, beheading their pretender king and more than twenty-eight hundred persons down to the rank of ten-thousand-household chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he captured the tribal forces of Yishan and neighboring counties, executing their self-proclaimed king and more than 2,800 subordinates down to the rank of ten-thousand-household chief.

sentences.zh: 以征南左副將軍從都督楊文討龍州土官趙宗壽，宗壽伏罪。

translations.literal: As left vice general of the southern expedition he followed Commissioner Yang Wen against the native official Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou; Zongshou submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as left vice general of the southern expedition, he followed Commissioner Yang Wen against Zhao Zongshou, the native official of Longzhou, who then submitted to judgment.

sentences.zh: 移兵征南丹、奉議及都康、向武、富勞、上林、思恩、都亮諸蠻，先後斬獲萬余級。

translations.literal: He shifted his forces to campaign against the tribes of Nandan, Fengyi, Dukang, Xiangwu, Fulao, Shanglin, Si'en, Duliang, and others, beheading and capturing in all more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army against the tribes of Nandan, Fengyi, Dukang, Xiangwu, Fulao, Shanglin, Si'en, Duliang, and other districts, killing and capturing more than 10,000 in successive operations.

sentences.zh: 觀生長兵間，有勇略。

translations.literal: Guan grew up amid warfare and possessed courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had grown up in the field and was both brave and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 性鷙悍，誅罰無所假。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and harsh; in punishment he showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature fierce and relentless, granting no quarter in punishment.

sentences.zh: 下令如山，人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: His orders were immovable as mountains; none dared transgress them.
translations.idiomatic: His commands stood firm as mountains, and no one dared defy them.

sentences.zh: 初，群蠻所在蜂起，剽郡縣，殺守吏，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: At first the various tribes rose everywhere like swarming bees, plundering prefectures and counties and killing defending officials; their power was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: At first the tribal peoples had risen everywhere, raiding prefectures and counties, killing local officials, and growing alarmingly powerful.

sentences.zh: 將士畏觀法，爭死鬥。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers feared Guan's discipline and vied to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and men feared his discipline and fought one another to die first in battle.

sentences.zh: 觀得賊必處以極刑。

translations.literal: Whenever Guan captured bandits he invariably inflicted extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Guan captured rebels he invariably punished them with the utmost severity.

sentences.zh: 間縱一二，使歸告諸蠻，諸蠻膽落。

translations.literal: Occasionally he released one or two to return and report to the tribes, and the tribes' courage collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Now and then he would release a captive or two to carry word back to the tribes, and their courage collapsed.

sentences.zh: 由是境內得安。

translations.literal: Thereby the territory within the borders was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the region was brought to peace.

sentences.zh: 二十九年召還，進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was recalled and promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he was recalled and promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年復從楊文討平吉州及五開叛苗，與顧成討平水西諸蠻堡，還理左府事。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed Yang Wen to pacify the rebel Miao of Jizhou and Wukai, and with Gu Cheng pacified the tribal stockades of Shuixi, then returned to manage affairs of the Left Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again followed Commissioner Yang Wen in pacifying the rebel Miao of Jizhou and Wukai, and with Gu Cheng subdued the Shuixi tribal stockades before returning to manage the left military commission.

sentences.zh: 建文元年練兵德州，禦燕師無功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he drilled troops at Dezhou and defended against Yan's army without success.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 1 he drilled troops at Dezhou and tried to hold off the Yan army, but without success.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，委任如故。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu emperor acceded, his appointments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu emperor acceded, his appointments remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 命往江西練軍城守，兼節制廣東、福建、湖廣三都司。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Jiangxi to drill troops and defend the city, and concurrently to command the three regional commands of Guangdong, Fujian, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Jiangxi to drill troops and hold the city, while concurrently commanding the regional commands of Guangdong, Fujian, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 廬陵民嘯聚山澤。

translations.literal: The people of Luling gathered in the mountains and marshes with war cries.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Luling had banded together in the hills and marshes.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲用兵，遣行人許子謨賫敕招諭，命觀臨撫之。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to use troops; he sent the itinerant official Xu Zimo bearing an edict to summon and instruct them, and ordered Guan to go and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to resort to arms and sent the itinerant official Xu Zimo with an edict of summons and reassurance, ordering Guan to go and pacify the people on the spot.

sentences.zh: 觀至，眾皆復業，賜璽書褒勞。

translations.literal: When Guan arrived, the multitude all returned to their occupations, and he was granted an imperial missive of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan arrived the people all returned to their livelihoods, and the court rewarded him with an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 命佩征南將軍印，鎮廣西，節制兩廣官軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the South, garrison Guangxi, and command the regular forces of the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to wear the seal of the southern-pacification general, to garrison Guangxi, and to command the regular armies of both Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 帝知觀嗜殺，賜璽書戒之曰：「蠻民易叛難服，殺愈多愈不治。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Guan was addicted to killing and sent an imperial missive admonishing him, saying: "Tribal peoples are quick to rebel and hard to pacify; the more you kill, the less governable they become.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Guan's appetite for bloodshed, the emperor sent him an imperial letter of warning: "Tribal peoples rebel easily and submit with difficulty; the more you kill, the harder they are to govern.

sentences.zh: 卿往鎮，務綏懷之，毋專殺戮。」

translations.literal: When you take up your post, strive to soothe and win them over; do not rely on slaughter alone."
translations.idiomatic: When you take up your command, win them through reassurance and care; do not rely on killing alone."

sentences.zh: 會群蠻復叛，帝遣員外郎李宗輔賫敕招之。

translations.literal: Just then the various tribes rebelled again, and the Emperor sent the bureau vice director Li Zongfu bearing an edict to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the tribes rebelled again, and the emperor sent Vice Director Li Zongfu of the Ministry of Revenue with an edict to summon them back.

sentences.zh: 觀大陳兵示將發狀，而遣使與宗輔俱。

translations.literal: Guan arrayed his troops on a grand scale to show that he was about to march, yet sent an envoy to go with Zongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan massed his troops in a show of imminent advance, yet sent an envoy to accompany Zongfu.

sentences.zh: 桂林蠻復業者六千家，惟思恩蠻未附。

translations.literal: Six thousand households of Guilin tribes returned to their occupations; only the Si'en tribes had not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand Guilin tribal households returned to their livelihoods, but the Si'en tribes had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 而慶遠、柳、潯諸蠻方殺掠吏民，乃上章請討。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the tribes of Qingyuan, Liu, and Xun were killing and plundering officials and commoners, so he memorialized requesting a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the tribes of Qingyuan, Liuzhou, and Xunzhou were killing and plundering officials and civilians, and he memorialized the throne requesting authorization to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年與指揮葛森等擊斬理定諸縣山賊千一百八十有奇，擒其酋五十余人，斬以徇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, together with Commander Ge Sen and others, he attacked and beheaded more than eleven hundred and eighty mountain bandits of Liding and other counties, captured more than fifty of their chiefs, and executed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1, together with Commander Ge Sen and others, he attacked and killed more than 1,180 mountain bandits in Liding and neighboring counties, captured more than fifty chieftains, and executed them publicly as a warning.

sentences.zh: 還所掠男女於民，而撫輯其逃散者。

translations.literal: He returned the men and women who had been seized to the people and soothed and gathered those who had fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He restored captives to their families and brought back those who had fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 明年遣都指揮朱輝諭降宜山、忻城諸山寨。

translations.literal: The next year he sent Regional Commander Zhu Hui to summon the mountain stockades of Yishan, Xincheng, and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent Regional Commander Zhu Hui to persuade the mountain strongholds of Yishan and Xincheng to submit.

sentences.zh: 荔波瑤震恐，乞為編戶。

translations.literal: The Yao of Libo were terrified and begged to be registered as regular households.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Libo were terrified and petitioned to be registered as regular tax-paying households.

sentences.zh: 帝屬觀撫之，八十余洞皆歸附。

translations.literal: The Emperor entrusted Guan to pacify them, and more than eighty cave settlements all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Guan with pacifying them, and more than eighty cave settlements submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 明年，潯、桂、柳三府蠻作亂，已撫復叛，遣朱輝以偏師破之。

translations.literal: The next year the tribes of the three prefectures of Xun, Gui, and Liu rebelled; though once pacified they rebelled again, and he sent Zhu Hui with a detached force to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the tribes of Xun, Gui, and Liuzhou prefectures rose again—having submitted once, they rebelled anew—and he sent Zhu Hui with a secondary column to break them.

sentences.zh: 蠻大懼。

translations.literal: The tribes were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were terrified.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣郎中徐子良至，遂來降，歸所掠人畜器械。

translations.literal: Just then the court sent Director Xu Ziliang, and they came to surrender, returning the people, livestock, and weapons they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: When the court dispatched Director Xu Ziliang they submitted, returning the people, livestock, and weapons they had seized.

sentences.zh: 四年大發兵討安南，詔觀畫方略，轉粟二十萬石餉軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year a great force was raised to campaign against Annam; Guan was ordered to draft strategy and transport two hundred thousand piculs of grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the court mobilized a major expedition against Annam, ordering Guan to plan strategy and transport 200,000 piculs of grain to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 已，復命偕大理卿陳洽選土兵三萬會太平，仍令觀偵安南賊中動靜。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was again ordered, together with Chief Minister of Justice Chen Qia, to select thirty thousand native troops to assemble at Taiping, and Guan was still charged to spy on movements within the Annamese rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered, together with Chief Minister of Justice Chen Qia, to raise thirty thousand native troops for assembly at Taiping, while Guan continued to reconnoiter enemy movements in Annam.

sentences.zh: 尋從大兵發憑祥，抵坡壘關，以所部營關下，伐木治橋梁，給軍食。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the main army from Pingxiang, reaching Polei Pass; he encamped his division below the pass, felled timber to repair bridges, and supplied the army with food.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he marched with the main army from Pingxiang to Polei Pass, encamped his division below the pass, cut timber to build bridges, and provisioned the army.

sentences.zh: 安南平，命措置交阯緣途諸堡，而柳、潯諸蠻乘觀出，復叛。

translations.literal: When Annam was pacified he was ordered to arrange the various forts along the Jiaozhi route, but the tribes of Liu, Xun, and others took advantage of Guan's absence to rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: After Annam was pacified he was ordered to organize the frontier forts along the Jiaozhi route, but the tribes of Liuzhou and Xunzhou rebelled again while Guan was away.

sentences.zh: 五年，觀旋師抵柳州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guan returned with his army and reached Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Guan marched back and reached Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊望風遁匿，觀請俟秋涼深入，且請濟師。

translations.literal: The bandits fled at the sight of his banners; Guan requested to wait until the cool of autumn to penetrate deeply, and also requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled at the first rumor of his approach; Guan asked to wait for cooler autumn weather before pushing deep into the hills and requested additional troops.

sentences.zh: 帝使使發湖廣、廣東、貴州三都司兵，又敕新城侯張輔遣都督朱廣、方政以征交阯兵協討。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to mobilize troops from the three regional commands of Huguang, Guangdong, and Guizhou, and also ordered Marquis Zhang Fu of Xincheng to dispatch Commissioners Zhu Guang and Fang Zheng with the Annam expeditionary forces to join the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched envoys to mobilize troops from the Huguang, Guangdong, and Guizhou regional commands and ordered Marquis Zhang Fu of Xincheng to send Commissioners Zhu Guang and Fang Zheng with the Annam expeditionary army to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 十月，諸軍皆集，分道進剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month all armies assembled and advanced by separate routes to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month all forces assembled and advanced along separate routes to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 觀自以貴州、兩廣兵由柳州攻馬平、來賓、遷江、賓州、上林、羅城、融縣，皆破之。

translations.literal: Guan himself led the Guizhou and two-Guang forces from Liuzhou to attack Maping, Laibin, Qianjiang, Binzhou, Shanglin, Luocheng, and Rong county, and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: Guan himself led the Guizhou and two-Guang forces from Liuzhou against Maping, Laibin, Qianjiang, Binzhou, Shanglin, Luocheng, and Rong county, defeating them all.

sentences.zh: 會兵象州，復進武宣、東鄉、桂林、貴平、永福。

translations.literal: He joined forces at Xiangzhou and advanced again on Wuxuan, Dongxiang, Guilin, Guiping, and Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: He concentrated his forces at Xiangzhou and advanced on Wuxuan, Dongxiang, Guilin, Guiping, and Yongfu.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬餘級，擒萬三千餘人，群蠻復定。

translations.literal: Heads taken exceeded ten thousand; more than thirteen thousand were captured; the various tribes were pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: More than 10,000 heads were taken and more than 13,000 captives seized, and the tribal peoples were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝嘉勞之。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the Emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When word of victory reached the court, the emperor commended and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 九年拜征夷副將軍，仍佩故印，總兵鎮交阯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Vice General Who Subdues the Barbarians, still wearing his former seal, with overall command garrisoning Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was appointed vice general for the subjugation of the barbarians, retained his former seal, and took overall command of the garrison in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 明年復命轉粟給張輔軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was again ordered to transport grain to supply Zhang Fu's army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again ordered to transport grain for Zhang Fu's army.

sentences.zh: 輔再出師定交阯，觀皆主饋運，不為將，故功不著。

translations.literal: When Fu again took the field to pacify Jiaozhi, Guan was always in charge of supply transport and did not serve as a field commander, so his achievements were not prominent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fu marched again to secure Jiaozhi, Guan was always responsible for logistics rather than field command, so his martial credit remained modest.

sentences.zh: 觀在廣西久，威震南中，蠻人惴惴奉命。

translations.literal: Guan had long been in Guangxi; his awesomeness shook the southern regions, and the tribes submitted in trembling obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had long served in Guangxi, and his reputation awed the south; the tribal peoples obeyed in fear and trembling.

sentences.zh: 繼之者，自山雲外，皆不能及。

translations.literal: Those who succeeded him, apart from Shan Yun, could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who followed him, none but Shan Yun could approach his record.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月卒，無子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year he died, leaving no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of year 12, leaving no son.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，保定伯梁銘奏求觀南京故宅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, Earl Liang Ming of Baoding memorialized requesting Guan's former residence in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 2, Earl Liang Ming of Baoding memorialized requesting Guan's former house in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 既聞觀妻居其中，曰：「觀，功臣地，雖歿，豈可奪之？」

translations.literal: When he learned that Guan's wife still lived there, he said: "Guan was a meritorious minister; though dead, how can his dwelling be taken away?"
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Guan's widow still lived there, he said: "Guan was a meritorious minister. Though he is dead, how can we seize his home?"

sentences.zh: 遂不許。

translations.literal: He therefore did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore refused.

sentences.zh: 令有司以他宅賜銘。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials to grant Ming another residence.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to grant Ming a different house instead.

sentences.zh: 山雲，徐人。

translations.literal: Shan Yun was a man of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Yun came from Xu.

sentences.zh: 父青，以百戶從成祖起兵，積功至都督僉事。

translations.literal: His father Qing, as a centurion, followed Chengzu in raising the army and through accumulated merit reached vice commissioner of the chief military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing had followed the Chengzu emperor's uprising as a centurion and rose through merit to vice commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 雲貌魁梧，多智略。

translations.literal: Yun was tall and imposing in appearance and possessed much wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was tall and imposing and possessed considerable strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 初襲金吾左衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At first he inherited the post of commander of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited the post of commander of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 數從出塞，有功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns beyond the frontier and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned beyond the frontier on many occasions and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 時幼軍二十五所，隸府軍前衛，掌衛者不任事，更命雲及李玉等五人撫戢之。

translations.literal: At the time there were twenty-five juvenile-army posts subordinate to the Forward Guard of the Metropolitan Garrison; those in charge of the guard were not equal to their duties, so Yun and Li Yu and four others were reassigned to pacify and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time twenty-five juvenile-army companies were attached to the Forward Metropolitan Guard, but their commanders were incompetent, so Yun, Li Yu, and four others were reassigned to discipline them.

sentences.zh: 仁守立，擢行在中軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: His benevolence and uprightness were established, and he was promoted to vice commissioner of the mobile army in the chief military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His fair and upright administration won recognition, and he was promoted to vice commissioner of the mobile army at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年改北京行都督府，命偕都御史王彰自山海抵居庸，巡視關隘，以便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande the Beijing traveling regional command was reorganized; he was ordered, together with Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhang, from Shanhai to Juyong to inspect the passes and act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1, when the Beijing traveling regional command was reorganized, he was ordered with Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhang to inspect the frontier passes from Shanhai to Juyong and to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 帝征樂安，召輔鄭王、襄王居守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Le'an, he was summoned to assist the Princes of Zheng and Xiang in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Le'an, Yun was recalled to assist the princes of Zheng and Xiang in guarding the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，柳、慶蠻韋朝烈等掠臨桂諸縣。

translations.literal: The next year the tribes of Liu and Qing, Wei Chaolie and others, plundered the counties of Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wei Chaolie and other tribal leaders from Liuzhou and Qingyuan raided the counties around Lingui.

sentences.zh: 時鎮遠侯顧興祖以不救邱溫被逮，公侯大臣舉雲。

translations.literal: At the time Marquis Gu Xingzu of Zhenyuan was arrested for failing to rescue Qiu Wen; dukes, marquises, and chief ministers recommended Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Gu Xingzu of Zhenyuan had been arrested for failing to relieve Qiu Wen, and the highest nobles and ministers recommended Yun.

sentences.zh: 帝亦自知之。

translations.literal: The Emperor also knew this himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already knew Yun was the right man.

sentences.zh: 三年正月命佩征蠻將軍印，充總兵官往鎮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Tribes and serve as overall commander to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3 he was ordered to wear the seal of the tribal-pacification general and take overall command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 雲至，討朝烈，破之。

translations.literal: When Yun arrived he campaigned against Chaolie and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun arrived he attacked Chaolie and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 賊保山巔，山峻險，掛木於藤，壘石其上。

translations.literal: The bandits held the mountain summit; the mountain was steep and perilous; they hung timbers on vines and piled stones above.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the mountain crest; the peak was steep and dangerous, with timbers hung from vines and stones heaped above.

sentences.zh: 官軍至，輒斷藤下木石，無敢近者。

translations.literal: When government troops arrived, the vines were cut and timbers and stones came down; none dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever government troops approached, the vines were cut and timber and stone rained down, and no one dared come near.

sentences.zh: 雲夜半束火牛羊角，以金鼓隨其後，驅向賊。

translations.literal: At midnight Yun bound torches to ox and goat horns, followed them with gongs and drums, and drove them toward the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Yun tied torches to ox and goat horns, followed them with drums and gongs, and drove the herd toward the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊謂官軍至，亟斷藤。

translations.literal: The bandits thought government troops had arrived and hastily cut the vines.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought the army had arrived and hurriedly cut the vines.

sentences.zh: 比明，木石且盡，眾噪而登，遂盡破之。

translations.literal: By dawn the timber and stones were nearly exhausted; the troops shouted and climbed, and thus completely defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn their stock of timber and stone was nearly gone; Yun's men shouted and stormed the height, routing the rebels completely.

sentences.zh: 南安、廣源諸蠻悉下。

translations.literal: The tribes of Nan'an, Guangyuan, and others all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Nan'an, Guangyuan, and neighboring districts all submitted.

sentences.zh: 是夏，忻城蠻譚團作亂，雲討擒之。

translations.literal: That summer the Xincheng tribesman Tan Tuan rebelled; Yun campaigned against him and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Tan Tuan of the Xincheng tribes rebelled; Yun campaigned against him and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 四年春，討平柳、潯諸蠻。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he campaigned against and pacified the tribes of Liu, Xun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 4 he suppressed the tribes of Liuzhou and Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 其秋，雒容蠻出掠，遣指揮王綸破之。

translations.literal: That autumn the Luorong tribes came out to plunder; he sent Commander Wang Lun to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Luorong tribes raided outward; he sent Commander Wang Lun to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 雲上綸功，並劾其殺良民罪，帝宥綸而心重雲。

translations.literal: Yun reported Lun's achievements and also impeached him for killing innocent commoners; the Emperor pardoned Lun but valued Yun in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yun reported Lun's victories but also impeached him for killing innocent civilians; the emperor pardoned Lun but came to esteem Yun all the more.

sentences.zh: 廣西自韓觀卒後，諸蠻漸橫。

translations.literal: Since Han Guan's death in Guangxi, the various tribes had gradually grown arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Guan's death the tribal peoples of Guangxi had grown increasingly defiant.

sentences.zh: 雲以廣西兵少，留貴州兵為用，先後討平潯、柳、平樂、桂林、宜山、思恩諸蠻。

translations.literal: Because Guangxi had few troops, Yun retained Guizhou troops for use and in succession campaigned against and pacified the tribes of Xun, Liu, Pingle, Guilin, Yishan, Si'en, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Guangxi understrength, Yun kept Guizhou troops on hand and in succession pacified the tribes of Xunzhou, Liuzhou, Pingle, Guilin, Yishan, Si'en, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 九年又以慶遠、郁林苗、瑤非大創不服，請濟師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because the Miao and Yao of Qingyuan and Yulin would not submit without a major blow, he requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he reported that the Miao and Yao of Qingyuan and Yulin would not submit without a major defeat and requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔發廣東兵千五百人益雲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered fifteen hundred Guangdong troops sent to augment Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered 1,500 Guangdong troops sent to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 雲分道剿捕，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Yun pursued and captured by separate routes, taking and beheading very many.
translations.idiomatic: Yun pursued the rebels along separate routes, capturing and killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 復遣指揮田真攻大藤峽賊，破之。

translations.literal: He again sent Commander Tian Zhen to attack the bandits of Great Rattan Gorge and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Commander Tian Zhen against the rebels of Great Rattan Gorge and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 雲在鎮，先後大戰十余，斬首萬二千二百六十，降賊酋三百七十，奪還男女二千五百八十，築城堡十三，鋪舍五百，陶磚鑿石，增高益厚。

translations.literal: While Yun was in command he fought more than ten major battles in succession, beheading twelve thousand two hundred and sixty, accepting the surrender of three hundred and seventy bandit chiefs, recovering two thousand five hundred and eighty men and women, building thirteen forts and castles, five hundred outpost lodges, firing bricks and quarrying stone to raise and thicken the walls.
translations.idiomatic: During his command he fought more than ten major engagements, taking 12,260 heads, receiving the surrender of 370 rebel chiefs, recovering 2,580 captives, building thirteen forts, erecting five hundred outpost stations, and firing bricks and quarrying stone to raise and thicken the defenses.

sentences.zh: 自是瑤、僮屏跡，居民安堵。

translations.literal: From this the Yao and Zhuang withdrew from sight, and the inhabitants lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Yao and Zhuang vanished from the roads, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 論功，進都督同知，璽書褒勞。

translations.literal: In accounting for merit, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, and an imperial seal letter commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When his merits were assessed, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and received an imperial letter of commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 雲謀勇深沈，而端潔不茍取，公賞罰，嚴號令，與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Yun was deep in strategy and courage, yet upright and clean and not grasping in acceptance; he was fair in rewards and punishments, strict in commands, and shared hardship and ease with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was shrewd and courageous in counsel, upright and incorruptible, fair in reward and punishment, firm in his orders, and shared every hardship with his men.

sentences.zh: 臨機應變，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: Facing the moment he adapted and changed; in battle there was none he did not win.
translations.idiomatic: He adapted swiftly to circumstances, and in battle he was invariably victorious.

sentences.zh: 廣西鎮帥初至，土官率饋獻為故事。

translations.literal: When a commander newly arrived in Guangxi, native officials invariably presented gifts as custom.
translations.idiomatic: When a military commissioner first arrived in Guangxi, native officials invariably offered gifts as a matter of custom.

sentences.zh: 帥受之，即為所持。

translations.literal: If the commander accepted them, he was immediately held in their grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Once a commander accepted such gifts, the donors held leverage over him.

sentences.zh: 雲始至，聞府吏鄭牢剛直，召問曰：「饋可受乎？」

translations.literal: When Yun had just arrived, hearing that the prefectural clerk Zheng Lao was upright and firm, he summoned and asked him, saying: "May gifts be accepted?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yun first arrived, he heard that the prefectural clerk Zheng Lao was upright and resolute. He summoned him and asked, "Should I accept these gifts?"

sentences.zh: 牢曰：「潔衣被體，一汙不可湔，將軍新潔衣也。」

translations.literal: Lao said: "Clean clothes on the body—once stained they cannot be washed clean; the general is in newly clean clothes."
translations.idiomatic: Lao replied, "Clean garments worn on the body—stain them once and they can never be fully washed. You are still in fresh, unsullied garb, General."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「不受，彼且生疑，奈何？」

translations.literal: Yun said: "If I do not accept them, they will become suspicious—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "If I refuse them, they will grow suspicious. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 牢曰：「黷貨，法當死。

translations.literal: Lao said: "Accepting goods corruptly—by law one ought to die.
translations.idiomatic: Lao said, "Taking bribes is a capital offense under the law.

sentences.zh: 將軍不畏天子法，乃畏土夷乎？」

translations.literal: The general does not fear the Son of Heaven's law, yet fears the native tribes?"
translations.idiomatic: You do not fear the emperor's law, yet you fear the native chiefs?"

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 盡卻饋獻，嚴馭之。

translations.literal: He rejected all gifts entirely and governed them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift offered and enforced strict discipline thereafter.

sentences.zh: 由是土官畏服，調發無敢後者。

translations.literal: From this the native officials feared and submitted; in mobilization none dared delay.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the native officials submitted in awe, and none dared lag when called to mobilize.

sentences.zh: 雲所至，詢問裏老，撫善良，察誣枉，土人皆愛之。

translations.literal: Wherever Yun went, he inquired of the village elders, comforted the good and kind, and examined false accusations and wrongs; the native people all loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yun went he consulted village elders, cared for the worthy, investigated false accusations and injustice, and won the affection of the local people.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，雲墜馬傷股。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Yun fell from his horse and injured his thigh.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Yun fell from his horse and injured his thigh.

sentences.zh: 帝遣醫馳視。

translations.literal: The emperor sent physicians posthaste to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent physicians posthaste to treat him.

sentences.zh: 以病請代，優詔不許。

translations.literal: He requested relief on grounds of illness, but a gracious edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved on account of illness, but a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統二年上言：「潯州與大藤峽諸山相錯，瑤寇出沒，占耕旁近田。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 2 he memorialized: "Xunzhou borders the mountains of Dateng Gorge; Yao bandits come and go, occupying and farming nearby fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengtong he memorialized: "Xunzhou lies among the mountains of Dateng Gorge, where Yao raiders come and go, seizing and farming nearby fields.

sentences.zh: 左右兩江土官，所屬人多田少。

translations.literal: The native officials along the Left and Right rivers have many subjects but little land.
translations.idiomatic: The native officials along the Left and Right rivers have large populations but little land.

sentences.zh: 其狼兵素勇，為賊所畏。

translations.literal: Their Lang militia are by nature brave and are feared by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Their Lang militia are naturally fierce fighters, and the bandits fear them.

sentences.zh: 若量撥田州土兵於近山屯種，分界耕守，斷賊出入。

translations.literal: If a measured allotment of Tianzhou native troops were posted to farm garrisons in the nearby hills, with boundaries set for cultivation and defense to cut off the bandits' movements in and out,
translations.idiomatic: If native troops from Tianzhou were posted in measured numbers to farm garrison fields in the nearby hills, with boundaries set for cultivation and defense to block the bandits' movements,

sentences.zh: 不過數年，賊必坐困。」

translations.literal: within a few years the bandits will inevitably be worn down by attrition."
translations.idiomatic: within a few years the bandits will inevitably be worn down by attrition."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 嗣後東南有急，輒調用狼兵，自此始也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever the southeast faced an emergency, Lang militia were mobilized — a practice that began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the southeast faced an emergency, Lang militia were mobilized — a practice that began from this time.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: The next winter he died in command.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈懷遠伯，謚忠毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Earl of Huaiyuan with the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Earl of Huaiyuan with the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 長子俊，襲府軍前衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jun inherited the post of commander of the Forward Metropolitan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jun inherited the post of commander of the Forward Metropolitan Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣西人思雲不置，立祠肖像祀焉。

translations.literal: The people of Guangxi missed Yun incessantly and erected a shrine with his portrait for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangxi missed Yun deeply and erected a shrine with his portrait for worship.

sentences.zh: 初，韓觀鎮廣西，專殺戮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Guan commanded Guangxi and devoted himself to killing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Guan had commanded Guangxi, he had dealt almost exclusively in executions.

sentences.zh: 慶遠諸生來迓。

translations.literal: The student-scholars of Qingyuan came to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The student-scholars of Qingyuan came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 觀曰：「此皆賊覘我也。」

translations.literal: Guan said: "These are all bandits spying on me."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "These are all rebel scouts."

sentences.zh: 悉斬之。

translations.literal: He had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 雲平恕，參佐有罪，輒上請，不妄殺人，人亦不敢犯。

translations.literal: Yun was even-tempered and forgiving; when subordinates had offenses he always submitted a request upward and did not kill people recklessly, and people also did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was even-tempered and merciful. When a subordinate committed an offense he always reported it to the court rather than killing recklessly, and as a result no one dared transgress.

sentences.zh: 鄭牢嘗逮事觀。

translations.literal: Zheng Lao had once served under Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lao had once served under Guan.

sentences.zh: 觀醉，輒殺人。

translations.literal: When Guan was drunk he would immediately kill people.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan grew drunk he would kill people on the spot.

sentences.zh: 牢輒留之，醒乃以白。

translations.literal: Lao would always detain them; only when Guan sobered would he report it.
translations.idiomatic: Lao would hold the condemned back and only inform Guan once he had sobered.

sentences.zh: 牢為士大夫所重，然竟以隸終。

translations.literal: Lao was esteemed by scholar-officials, yet in the end he died as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Lao was held in esteem by the gentry, yet he ended his days as a mere clerk.

sentences.zh: 蕭授，華容人。

translations.literal: Xiao Shou was a man of Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shou came from Huarong.

sentences.zh: 由千戶從成祖起兵，至都指揮同知。

translations.literal: From thousand-household he followed the Chengzu emperor in raising the army, rising to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a thousand-household officer, he followed the Chengzu emperor when he raised his army and rose to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 永樂十六年擢右軍都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮湖廣、貴州。

translations.literal: In Yongle year 16 he was promoted to assistant commissioner of the Right Army and appointed commander-in-chief, garrisoning Huguang and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Yongle he was promoted to assistant commissioner of the Right Army, appointed commander-in-chief, and posted to garrison Huguang and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，鎮遠邛水蠻銀總作亂。

translations.literal: In Xuande year 1 the Qiongshui tribesman Yin Zong of Zhenyuan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande the Qiongshui tribesman Yin Zong of Zhenyuan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 指揮祝貴往撫，被殺。

translations.literal: The commander Zhu Gui went to pacify him and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhu Gui went to pacify him and was killed.

sentences.zh: 授遣都指揮張名破斬之。

translations.literal: Shou sent the commander-in-chief Zhang Ming to defeat and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sent Commander-in-Chief Zhang Ming to defeat and kill him.

sentences.zh: 貴州宣慰所轄乖西、巴香諸峒寨，山箐深險，諸蠻錯居。

translations.literal: The stockades of Guaixi, Baxiang, and other districts under the Guizhou pacification commission lay in deep and perilous mountain ravines where the tribes were intermixed.
translations.idiomatic: The stockades of Guaixi, Baxiang, and other districts under the Guizhou pacification commission lay in deep, perilous ravines where the tribes were intermixed.

sentences.zh: 攻剽他部，傷官軍，發民冢。

translations.literal: They raided other districts, wounded government troops, and opened commoners' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: They raided neighboring districts, wounded government troops, and desecrated commoners' graves.

sentences.zh: 而昆阻比諸寨亦恃險不輸賦。

translations.literal: The stockades of Kunzubi also relied on their terrain and refused to pay taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The stockades of Kunzubi likewise relied on their terrain and refused to pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 二年，授遣都指揮蘇保會宣慰宋斌攻破昆阻比寨，窮追，斬偽王以下數百人。

translations.literal: In year 2 Shou sent the commander-in-chief Su Bao together with Pacification Commissioner Song Bin to storm the Kunzubi stockades, pursued to the end, and beheaded several hundred persons down to the pretender king.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Shou sent Commander-in-Chief Su Bao with Pacification Commissioner Song Bin to storm the Kunzubi stockades, pursued relentlessly, and killed several hundred people down to the pretender king.

sentences.zh: 乖西諸蠻皆震懾歸命。

translations.literal: All the Guaixi tribes were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: All the Guaixi tribes were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 水西蠻阿閉妨宜作亂，授結旁寨酋，以計誅之。

translations.literal: The Shuixi tribesman A Bi Fang Yi rebelled; Shou won over chiefs of neighboring stockades and by stratagem executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shuixi tribesman A Bi Fang Yi rebelled, Shou won over chiefs of neighboring stockades and by stratagem had him killed.

sentences.zh: 而西堡蠻阿骨等與寨底、豐寧、清平、平越、普安諸苗復相聚為寇，四川筠連諸蠻應之。

translations.literal: Then the Xibao tribesmen A Gu and others together with the Miao of Zaidi, Fengning, Qingping, Pingyue, Pu'an, and other districts again gathered as bandits, and the tribes of Junlian in Sichuan responded.
translations.idiomatic: The Xibao tribesmen A Gu and others then joined with the Miao of Zaidi, Fengning, Qingping, Pingyue, Pu'an, and other districts to raid once more, and the tribes of Junlian in Sichuan rose in response.

sentences.zh: 授且捕且撫。

translations.literal: Shou both captured and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shou combined pursuit with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻先後聽命，承制赦之。

translations.literal: The various tribes in succession obeyed orders; by imperial authorization he pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes submitted one after another, and by imperial mandate he granted them pardon.

sentences.zh: 以豐寧酋稔惡，械送京師，伏誅。

translations.literal: Because the Fengning chief had long been wicked, he was sent shackled to the capital and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengning chief, guilty of longstanding offenses, was sent shackled to the capital and executed.

sentences.zh: 七年諭降安隆酋岑俊。

translations.literal: In year 7 he persuaded and accepted the surrender of the Anlong chief Cen Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he received the surrender of the Anlong chief Cen Jun.

sentences.zh: 已，討辰州蠻，擒其酋八十，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: Thereafter he campaigned against the Chenzhou tribes, capturing eighty of their chiefs and beheading and taking heads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned against the Chenzhou tribes, capturing eighty chiefs and killing countless others.

sentences.zh: 移兵擊江華苗，討富川山賊，先後破擒之。

translations.literal: He moved troops to strike the Jianghua Miao and campaigned against the mountain bandits of Fuchuan, defeating and capturing them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his forces against the Jianghua Miao and the mountain bandits of Fuchuan, defeating and capturing them in succession.

sentences.zh: 先是，貴州治古、答意二長官司苗數出掠。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Miao of the two native-office districts of Zhigu and Dayi in Guizhou had repeatedly come out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Miao under the Zhigu and Dayi native offices in Guizhou had repeatedly raided outward.

sentences.zh: 授築二十四堡，環其地，分兵以戍，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: Shou built twenty-four forts encircling their territory, distributed troops to garrison them, and the bandits could not act.
translations.idiomatic: Shou built twenty-four forts ringing their territory, posted troops to garrison them, and the rebels could no longer operate freely.

sentences.zh: 久之，其酋吳不爾覘官軍少，復掠清浪，殺官吏。

translations.literal: After a long time their chief Wu Bu'er, observing that government troops were few, again plundered Qinglang and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: After some time their chief Wu Bu'er, seeing that government forces were thinly spread, raided Qinglang again and killed local officials.

sentences.zh: 授遣張名擊破之。

translations.literal: Shou sent Zhang Ming to strike and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sent Zhang Ming to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 賊走湖廣境，結生苗，勢復張。

translations.literal: The bandits fled into Huguang territory, allied with the sheng Miao, and their power revived.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Huguang, allied with the unassimilated Miao, and grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 授乃發黔、楚、蜀軍分道捕討。

translations.literal: Shou then mobilized troops from Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan to pursue and punish along separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then mobilized troops from Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan to hunt them down along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 進軍筸子坪，誅不爾，斬首五百九十余級，賊悉平。

translations.literal: Advancing to Gangziping he executed Bu'er, beheading more than five hundred and ninety, and the bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Gangziping, he executed Wu Bu'er, took more than 590 heads, and pacified the rebels completely.

sentences.zh: 九年，都勻蠻為亂，引廣西賊入掠。

translations.literal: In year 9 the Duyun tribes rebelled and drew in Guangxi bandits to enter and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the Duyun tribes rebelled and brought in Guangxi raiders to loot the region.

sentences.zh: 授遣指揮陳原、顧勇分道邀擊，獲賊首韋萬良等，降下合江蔡郎等五十余寨。

translations.literal: Shou sent the commanders Chen Yuan and Gu Yong to intercept along separate routes, capturing the bandit chiefs Wei Wanliang and others and accepting the surrender of more than fifty stockades including Hejiang and Cailang.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sent the commanders Chen Yuan and Gu Yong to intercept them along separate routes, capturing the rebel leaders Wei Wanliang and others and receiving the submission of more than fifty stockades, including Hejiang and Cailang.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，命佩征蠻副將軍印，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Shou was ordered to wear the seal of deputy tribal-pacification general and continue in command as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Shou was ordered to wear the seal of deputy tribal-pacification general and continue in command as before.

sentences.zh: 念授年老，以都督僉事吳亮副之。

translations.literal: Considering that Shou was old, Assistant Commissioner Wu Liang was appointed as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shou was growing old, Assistant Commissioner Wu Liang was appointed as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，普定蠻阿遲等叛，僭稱王，四出攻掠。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 1 the Puding tribesman A Chi and others rebelled, arrogated the title of king, and raided in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong the Puding tribesman A Chi and others rebelled, proclaimed themselves kings, and raided in all directions.

sentences.zh: 授遣顧勇等搗其巢，破之。

translations.literal: Shou sent Gu Yong and others to strike their lair and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sent Gu Yong and others to strike their stronghold and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 而廣西蒙顧十六洞與湖廣逃民相聚蜂起，授督兵圍之。

translations.literal: Then the sixteen caves of Menggu in western Guangxi joined with fugitives from Huguang to rise like swarming bees; Shou led troops to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: Then the sixteen caves of Menggu in western Guangxi joined with fugitives from Huguang to rise in rebellion; Shou led troops to surround them.

sentences.zh: 再戰，悉擒斬其酋，余黨就誅。

translations.literal: After a second battle he captured and beheaded all their chiefs, and the remaining followers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: After a second battle he captured and beheaded all their chiefs, and the remaining followers were executed.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進右都督。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上言：「靖州與廣西接壤，時苦苗患。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Jingzhou borders Guangxi and has long suffered from Miao troubles.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Jingzhou borders Guangxi and has long suffered from Miao troubles.

sentences.zh: 永樂、宣德間，嘗儲糧數萬石，備軍興。

translations.literal: During the Yongle and Xuande reigns, tens of thousands of piculs of grain were once stored there to prepare for military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle and Xuande reigns, tens of thousands of piculs of grain were once stored there for military emergencies.

sentences.zh: 比年儲糧少。

translations.literal: In recent years the stored grain has been scant.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the stored grain has been scant.

sentences.zh: 有警，發人徒轉輸，賊輒先覺，以故不能得賊。

translations.literal: When an alarm arises, laborers are mobilized to transport supplies, yet the bandits always learn of it first; for this reason the bandits cannot be caught.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arises, laborers are mobilized to transport grain, but the bandits always learn of it first, and for that reason they cannot be caught.

sentences.zh: 乞於清浪、靖州二衛，各增儲五萬石，庶緩急可借。」

translations.literal: I ask that each of the Qinglang and Jingzhou guards increase its stores by fifty thousand piculs, so that they may be drawn upon in urgent need."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each of the Qinglang and Jingzhou guards increase its stores by fifty thousand piculs, so that they may be drawn upon in urgent need."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，貴州計沙賊苗金蟲、苗總牌糾洪江生苗作亂，偽立「統千侯」、「統萬侯」號。

translations.literal: In year 4 the Jisha bandits in Guizhou, the Miao Jin Chong and Miao Zongpai, incited the Hongjiang sheng Miao to rebel and falsely established the titles "Lord of a Thousand Regiments" and "Lord of Myriad Regiments."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Jisha rebels—the Miao leaders Jin Chong and Zongpai—incited the Hongjiang sheng Miao to rise, proclaiming themselves "Lord of a Thousand Regiments" and "Lord of Myriad Regiments."

sentences.zh: 授督兵抵計沙，分遣都指揮鄭通攻三羊洞，馬曄攻黃柏山，大破之。

translations.literal: Shou led troops to Jisha, dispatched the commanders-in-chief Zheng Tong to attack Sanyang Cave and Ma Ye to attack Huangbo Mountain, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou marched on Jisha and sent the commanders-in-chief Zheng Tong against Sanyang Cave and Ma Ye against Huangbo Mountain, routing both forces.

sentences.zh: 吳亮窮追至蒲頭、洪江，斬總牌，千戶尹勝誘斬金蟲，於是生苗盡降。

translations.literal: Wu Liang pursued to exhaustion to Putou and Hongjiang, beheading Zongpai; the thousand-household Yin Sheng by inducement beheaded Jin Chong, and thus the sheng Miao all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Liang pursued the rebels to Putou and Hongjiang and killed Zongpai; the thousand-household officer Yin Sheng lured Jin Chong out and killed him, whereupon the sheng Miao surrendered entirely.

sentences.zh: 授沈毅多計算，裨校皆盡其材，而馭軍嚴整。

translations.literal: Shou was deep and resolute, abounding in stratagem; his staff officers all gave their fullest talents, yet his control of the army was strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was deliberate and resourceful, drawing the best from his officers while keeping his troops under iron discipline.

sentences.zh: 自鎮遠侯顧成歿，群蠻所在屯結。

translations.literal: Since the death of the Marquis of Zhenyuan, Gu Cheng, the various tribes had gathered everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Since the death of Gu Cheng, Marquis of Zhenyuan, the tribes had banded together wherever they could.

sentences.zh: 官軍討之，皆無功。

translations.literal: When government troops campaigned against them, all were without success.
translations.idiomatic: Government campaigns against them had all failed.

sentences.zh: 授在鎮二十余年，規畫多本於成。

translations.literal: Shou was in command for more than twenty years; his planning largely derived from Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shou held command for more than twenty years, and much of his strategy was drawn from Gu Cheng's experience.

sentences.zh: 久益明練，威信大行，寇起輒滅，前後諸帥莫及也。

translations.literal: Over time he grew ever more seasoned and practiced; his authority and trust widely prevailed, and when bandits arose he immediately extinguished them—commanders before and after could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew ever more seasoned with time. His authority became paramount, rebels were crushed as soon as they arose, and no commander before or since could equal him.

sentences.zh: 論功，進左都督。

translations.literal: In accounting for merit he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his merits were assessed he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是年六月召還，以老致仕。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month he was recalled, and on account of age retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the sixth month, he was recalled to court and retired on account of his age.

sentences.zh: 尋起視事右府。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed to administer affairs in the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to administer affairs in the Right Army commission.

sentences.zh: 十年卒。

translations.literal: In year 10 he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he died.

sentences.zh: 贈臨武伯，謚靖襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Linwu and given the posthumous title Jingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Linwu with the posthumous title Jingxiang.

sentences.zh: 吳亮，來安人。

translations.literal: Wu Liang was a man of Lai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Liang came from Lai'an.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，為旗手衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was assistant commander of the Qishou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he served as assistant commander of the Qishou Guard.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，署湖廣都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he served as acting assistant commander-in-chief of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he served as acting assistant commissioner-in-chief of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 尋以右副總兵與王瑜督漕運。

translations.literal: Soon as right vice commander-in-chief together with Wang Yu he supervised grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed right vice commander-in-chief and, together with Wang Yu, supervised the grain transport.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，討新淦賊有功，累進都督僉事，副授鎮湖廣、貴州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yingzong reign he campaigned against the Xin'gan bandits with merit and rose in succession to assistant commissioner-in-chief, then served as deputy to garrison Huguang and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingzong reign he earned distinction suppressing rebels in Xin'gan, was promoted in stages to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and was appointed deputy commander garrisoning Huguang and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 破普定蠻，進都督同知。

translations.literal: He defeated the Puding tribes and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Puding tribes he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 平計沙苗，進右都督。

translations.literal: He pacified the Jisha Miao and was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the Jisha Miao he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 方政歿於麓川，召亮還京，命為副總兵，將兵五萬往討。

translations.literal: Fang Zheng died at Lucchuan; Liang was recalled to the capital, appointed vice commander-in-chief, and ordered to lead fifty thousand troops to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Zheng died at Lucchuan, Liang was recalled to the capital, appointed vice commander-in-chief, and sent with fifty thousand men to carry on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至雲南，賊益熾，坐金齒參將張榮敗不救，逮下獄。

translations.literal: On reaching Yunnan the bandits grew fiercer; because the Jinchi deputy general Zhang Rong had been defeated and he did not rescue him, he was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yunnan he found the rebels stronger than ever. He was charged with failing to rescue the Jinchi deputy Zhang Rong after his defeat, arrested, and thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 左遷都督僉事，仍佩征南副將軍印，鎮湖廣、貴州，討平四川都掌蠻。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, yet still bore the seal of vice general of the southern expedition, garrisoned Huguang and Guizhou, and campaigned to pacify the Duzhang tribes of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, he retained the seal of vice general of the southern expedition, returned to garrison Huguang and Guizhou, and suppressed the Duzhang tribes of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，視右府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and administered affairs in the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to administer affairs in the Right Army commission.

sentences.zh: 正統十一年卒。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 11 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 亮姿貌魁梧，性寬簡，不喜殺戮，所至蠻人懷附。

translations.literal: Liang's appearance was imposing and stately; his nature was broad and plain, he did not like killing, and wherever he went the tribes attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was tall and imposing, open and easy in temperament, averse to slaughter; wherever he went the tribes welcomed his rule.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，至老，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: He loved reading; even to old age his hand never released a book.
translations.idiomatic: He was an avid reader and, even in old age, never put his books down.

sentences.zh: 方瑛，都督政之子。

translations.literal: Fang Ying was the son of Commissioner-in-Chief Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ying was the son of Commissioner-in-Chief Fang Zheng.

sentences.zh: 正統初，以舍人從父征麓川。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, as a household attendant he followed his father to campaign at Lucchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign he followed his father to Lucchuan as a household attendant.

sentences.zh: 父戰死，瑛發憤，矢報父仇。

translations.literal: His father died in battle; Ying burned with rage and vowed to avenge his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell in battle, Ying swore to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 初襲指揮使，已，論政死事功，遷都指揮同知。

translations.literal: At first he inherited the post of commander, and thereafter, in accounting for Zheng's death in service, he was transferred to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited his father's rank as commander, then, in recognition of Fang Zheng's death in service, was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六年從王驥征麓川。

translations.literal: In year 6 he followed Wang Ji to campaign at Lucchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he followed Wang Ji on the Lucchuan expedition.

sentences.zh: 帥兵六千突賊壘。

translations.literal: Leading six thousand troops he suddenly assaulted the bandit encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Leading six thousand men he stormed the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 賊渠衣黃衣帳中。

translations.literal: The bandit leader wore yellow robes in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain sat in his tent dressed in yellow.

sentences.zh: 瑛直前，左右擊斬數百人，躪死者無算，遂平其地。

translations.literal: Ying drove straight forward; those at his sides struck down and beheaded several hundred, and trampled dead were beyond counting; thus he pacified the place.
translations.idiomatic: Ying charged straight in. His men cut down several hundred rebels on either side and trampled countless others underfoot, and the stronghold was taken.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋復從驥破貢章、沙壩、阿嶺諸蠻。

translations.literal: Soon he again followed Ji to defeat the tribes of Gongzhang, Shaba, A'ling, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Ji again in defeating the tribes of Gongzhang, Shaba, A'ling, and others.

sentences.zh: 進都督僉事，蒞後府事，充右參將，協守雲南。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, took charge of affairs in the Rear Army, served as right deputy general, and jointly guarded Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, he took charge of the Rear Army commission, served as right deputy general, and helped defend Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十三年復從驥征麓川。

translations.literal: In year 13 he again followed Ji to campaign at Lucchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he again joined Wang Ji on the Lucchuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 破鬼山大寨，留鎮雲南。

translations.literal: He broke the great stockade at Guishan and remained to garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking the great stockade at Guishan he remained to garrison Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，廷議以瑛有將略，命都督毛福壽代，還，進都督同知。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 1 the court deliberated that Ying had military talent; he was ordered that Commissioner-in-Chief Mao Fushou replace him and return, and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai the court judged Ying to possess genuine military talent. Mao Fushou was appointed commissioner-in-chief in his place, Ying was recalled, and promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 甫抵京，而貴州群苗叛，道梗。

translations.literal: He had just reached the capital when the Miao of Guizhou rebelled en masse and the roads were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he reached the capital when the Miao of Guizhou rose in rebellion and cut the main routes.

sentences.zh: 驥請瑛還討。

translations.literal: Ji requested that Ying return to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji requested that Ying be sent back to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 其年四月拜右副總兵，與保定伯梁缶、侍郎侯琎次第破走之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year he was appointed right vice commander-in-chief; together with the Earl of Baoding, Liang Fou, and the vice minister Hou Jin he in succession defeated and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year he was appointed right vice commander-in-chief and, together with the Earl of Baoding Liang Fou and Vice Minister Hou Jin, drove the rebels back in successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 復破賞改諸寨，擒偽苗王王阿同等。

translations.literal: He again defeated the stockades of Shangai and others and captured the false Miao king Wang A'tong and others.
translations.idiomatic: He next broke the stockades around Shangai and captured the self-proclaimed Miao king Wang A'tong and others.

sentences.zh: 琎卒，都御史王來代督軍務，分道擊賊香爐山。

translations.literal: When Jin died, the censor-in-chief Wang Lai replaced him in supervising military affairs; they attacked the bandits at Xianglu Mountain along separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jin's death, Censor-in-Chief Wang Lai took over military command and they attacked the rebels at Xianglu Mountain along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 瑛入自龍場，大破平之。

translations.literal: Ying entered from Longchang and utterly defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Ying advanced through Longchang, routed the rebels, and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，來劾瑛違法事，置不問。

translations.literal: In the autumn of year 3 Lai impeached Ying for illegal matters; he was left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year 3 Wang Lai impeached Ying for misconduct, but the charge was dropped.

sentences.zh: 來召還，命瑛鎮守貴州。

translations.literal: Lai was recalled and Ying was ordered to garrison Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lai was recalled, and Ying was ordered to garrison Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬，討白石崖賊，俘斬二千五百人，招降四百六十寨。

translations.literal: That winter he campaigned against the bandits of White Stone Cliff, capturing and beheading two thousand five hundred, and accepting the surrender of four hundred and sixty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he suppressed the rebels at White Stone Cliff, killing or capturing 2,500 men and receiving the surrender of 460 stockades.

sentences.zh: 進左都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五年，四川草塘苗黃龍、韋保作亂，自稱「平天大王」，剽播州西坪、黃灘。

translations.literal: In year 5 the Caotang Miao of Sichuan, Huang Long and Wei Bao, rebelled, styled themselves "King Who Levels Heaven," and plundered Xiping and Huangtan in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Caotang Miao of Sichuan, Huang Long and Wei Bao, rebelled, proclaiming themselves "King Who Pacifies Heaven," and raided Xiping and Huangtan in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 瑛與巡撫蔣琳會川兵進剿，賊魁皆就縛。

translations.literal: Ying together with the grand coordinator Jiang Lin joined Sichuan troops in advancing to suppress; the bandit chiefs were all bound and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ying joined Grand Coordinator Jiang Lin and Sichuan troops in a joint campaign, and the rebel leaders were all captured.

sentences.zh: 因分兵克中潮山及三百灘、乖西、谷種、乖立諸寨，執偽王谷蟻丁等，斬首七千余。

translations.literal: Thereupon dividing troops he captured Zhongchao Mountain and the stockades of Sanbaitan, Guaixi, Guzhong, Guali, and others, seized the false king Gu Yiding and others, and beheaded more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his forces to take Zhongchao Mountain and the stockades at Sanbaitan, Guaixi, Guzhong, Guali, and elsewhere, capturing the self-proclaimed king Gu Yiding and others and taking more than 7,000 heads.

sentences.zh: 詔封南和伯。

translations.literal: An edict ennobled him as Earl of Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The court ennobled him as Earl of Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 瑛為將，嚴紀律，信賞罰，臨陣勇敢，善撫士。

translations.literal: As a general Ying was strict in discipline, trustworthy in reward and punishment, brave facing battle, and skilled at comforting soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Ying enforced strict discipline, kept his word in reward and punishment, fought bravely in the field, and knew how to win his men's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 士皆樂為用，以故數有功。

translations.literal: Soldiers all gladly served him; for this reason he repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: His men served him willingly, and as a result he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 廷臣言宜委以禁旅，乃召還，同石亨督京營軍務。

translations.literal: Court officials said he should be entrusted with the capital guard; he was then recalled and together with Shi Heng supervised the military affairs of the capital camp.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that he should be put in charge of the capital guard, so he was recalled to serve alongside Shi Heng in supervising the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 明年，琳奏瑛前守貴州，邊境寧，苗蠻畏服，乞遣還。

translations.literal: The next year Lin memorialized that Ying had formerly guarded Guizhou, the border was peaceful, and the Miao submitted in awe, and requested that he be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jiang Lin memorialized that when Ying had previously held Guizhou the frontier had been secure and the Miao had submitted in fear, and he asked that Ying be sent back.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，湖廣苗叛，拜瑛平蠻將軍，率京軍討之，而使御史張鵬偵其後。

translations.literal: Before long the Miao of Huguang rebelled; Ying was appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, led the capital army to campaign against them, and the censor Zhang Peng was sent to investigate behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Miao of Huguang rose in rebellion. Ying was appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, led the capital troops against them, and Censor Zhang Peng was dispatched to audit his conduct from the rear.

sentences.zh: 還奏，瑛所過秋毫不犯，帝大喜。

translations.literal: Returning to report, he said that everywhere Ying passed not even a hair of autumn grain was violated; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhang Peng reported that Ying's army had not harmed so much as a stalk of grain along the route, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 七年，賊渠蒙能攻平溪衛。

translations.literal: In year 7 the bandit chieftain Meng Neng attacked Pingxi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the rebel leader Meng Neng attacked Pingxi Guard.

sentences.zh: 都指揮鄭泰等擊卻之，能中火槍死，瑛遂進沅州。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Zheng Tai and others struck and repelled them; Neng was hit by a fire-lance and died, and Ying then advanced on Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Zheng Tai and others drove them back; Meng Neng was killed by a fire-lance, and Ying then advanced into Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 連破鬼板等一百六十余寨。

translations.literal: In succession he broke more than one hundred and sixty stockades including Guiban and others.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to take more than 160 stockades, including Guiban and others.

sentences.zh: 與尚書石璞移兵天柱，率陳友等分擊天堂諸寨，復大破之。

translations.literal: Together with the minister of war Shi Pu he moved troops to Tianzhu, led Chen You and others to attack separately the stockades of Tiantang and others, and again utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Minister of War Shi Pu in moving troops to Tianzhu, then led Chen You and others in separate attacks on the Tiantang stockades and routed the rebels once more.

sentences.zh: 克寨二百七十，擒偽侯伯以下一百二人。

translations.literal: He captured two hundred and seventy stockades and seized one hundred and two persons from false marquises and earls downward.
translations.idiomatic: He took 270 stockades and captured 102 self-styled nobles, from marquises and earls on down.

sentences.zh: 時英宗已復位。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yingzong had already been restored to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Yingzong had already been restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璞召還，瑛留鎮貴州、湖廣。

translations.literal: When news of victory was heard, Pu was recalled and Ying remained to garrison Guizhou and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory arrived, Shi Pu was recalled while Ying was left to garrison Guizhou and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 瑛討蒙能余黨，克銅鼓藕洞一百九十五寨，覃洞、上隆諸苗各斬其渠納款。

translations.literal: Ying campaigned against the remnant followers of Meng Neng, captured one hundred and ninety-five stockades of Tonggu and Oudong, and the Miao of Tandong, Shanglong, and others each beheaded their chiefs and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ying suppressed the remnants of Meng Neng's forces, taking 195 stockades at Tonggu and Oudong, while the Miao of Tandong, Shanglong, and elsewhere each executed their own leaders and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉瑛功，進侯。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Ying's merit and promoted him to marquess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Ying's achievements and promoted him to marquess.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，東苗幹把豬等僭偽號，攻都勻諸衛。

translations.literal: In Tianshun year 2 the eastern Miao Ganbazhu and others usurped false titles and attacked the guards of Duyun and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshun the eastern Miao leader Ganbazhu and others assumed false titles and attacked the guards around Duyun.

sentences.zh: 命瑛與巡撫白圭合川、湖、雲、貴軍討之，克六百余寨。

translations.literal: Ying was ordered together with the grand coordinator Bai Gui to combine the armies of Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou to campaign against them, and captured more than six hundred stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was ordered to join Grand Coordinator Bai Gui in combining forces from Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou against them, and they took more than 600 stockades.

sentences.zh: 邊方悉定。

translations.literal: The border regions were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 瑛前後克寨幾二千，俘斬四萬余。

translations.literal: Before and after, Ying captured stockades numbering nearly two thousand and captured or beheaded more than forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In all his campaigns Ying took nearly 2,000 stockades and killed or captured more than 40,000 enemies.

sentences.zh: 平苗之功，前此無與比者。

translations.literal: In the achievement of pacifying the Miao, none before this could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: No one before him had matched his record in pacifying the Miao.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於鎮，年四十五。

translations.literal: Soon he died at his post, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at his command post, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，賜謚忠襄。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken and grieved and granted the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and granted him the posthumous title Zhongxiang, "Loyal and Assisting."

sentences.zh: 瑛天姿英邁，曉古兵法。

translations.literal: Ying was naturally heroic and surpassing and understood ancient military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was naturally bold and gifted, and well versed in classical military strategy.

sentences.zh: 嘗上練兵法及陣圖，老將多稱之。

translations.literal: He once submitted methods of training troops and battle formations; veteran generals mostly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted treatises on drill and battle formations, which many veteran commanders praised.

sentences.zh: 為人廉，謙和不伐。

translations.literal: As a man he was incorruptible, modest, harmonious, and did not boast.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright, modest, and never boastful.

sentences.zh: 所至鎮以安靜，民思之，久而不忘。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived he garrisoned with tranquility; the people missed him and long did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he was posted he kept the region at peace, and the people remembered him long afterward.

sentences.zh: 子毅，嗣伯爵，誘祖母誣從父瑞不孝，坐奪爵閑住。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited the earldom, induced his grandmother to falsely accuse his uncle Rui of unfilial conduct, and was sentenced to deprivation of the title and idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the earldom but persuaded his grandmother to falsely accuse his uncle Rui of unfilial conduct; for this he was stripped of his title and reduced to private life.

sentences.zh: 卒，子壽祥嗣。

translations.literal: He died and his son Shouxiang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Shouxiang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷鎮貴州、湖廣。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era he successively garrisoned Guizhou and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served in turn as garrison commander of Guizhou and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: The transmitted title continued until the Ming perished and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued until the fall of the Ming, when it died out.

sentences.zh: 陳友，其先西域入，家全椒。

translations.literal: Chen You — his ancestors entered from the Western Regions and made their home at Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen You's family had come from the Western Regions and settled at Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 正統初，官千戶，累遷都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he held the office of chiliarch and was repeatedly promoted to assistant commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign he held the rank of chiliarch and rose through repeated promotions to assistant commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 頻年使瓦剌有勞，尋復進都指揮使。

translations.literal: Over successive years he served as envoy to the Oirats with merit and was soon again promoted to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as envoy to the Oirats with distinction and was soon promoted to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 九年充寧夏遊擊將軍，與總兵官黃真擊兀良哈。

translations.literal: In year 9 he served as mobile commander of Ningxia and together with the commander-in-chief Huang Zhen attacked the Urianghai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he served as mobile commander of Ningxia and, together with Commander-in-Chief Huang Zhen, fought the Urianghai.

sentences.zh: 多獲，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: He captured much and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took many captives and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出塞招答哈卜等四百人來歸。

translations.literal: Before long, going beyond the frontier he recruited Dahabi and four hundred others to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he crossed the frontier and persuaded Dahabi and four hundred others to come over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，進都督同知，征湖廣、貴州苗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing came to the throne he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and campaigned against the Miao of Huguang and Guizhou.
