translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi emperor acceded, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and sent against the Miao of Huguang and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋充左參將，守備靖州。

translations.literal: Soon he served as left deputy general and defended Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as left deputy general, defending Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年偕王來等擊賊香爐山，自萬潮山入，大破之。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 2 together with Wang Lai and others he attacked the bandits at Xianglu Mountain, entering from Wanchao Mountain, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he joined Wang Lai and others in attacking the rebels at Xianglu Mountain, advancing from Wanchao Mountain, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 留鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: He remained to garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He remained to garrison Huguang.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都督。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed and he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年春奏斬苗五百餘級，五年又奏斬苗三百餘。

translations.literal: In the spring of year 4 he memorialized that more than five hundred Miao heads had been taken; in year 5 he again memorialized that more than three hundred Miao had been beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 4 he reported more than 500 Miao killed; in year 5 he reported another 300 or more.

sentences.zh: 而都指揮戚安等八人戰死，兵部疑首功不實，指揮蔡升亦奏友欺妄。

translations.literal: Yet eight commanders-in-chief including Qi An died in battle; the Ministry of War suspected the reported head count was untrue, and the commander Cai Sheng also memorialized that You had deceived and lied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eight commanders, including Qi An, had died in battle; the Ministry of War doubted the reported kills, and Commander Cai Sheng also accused You of fraud.

sentences.zh: 命總督石璞廉之，斬獲僅三四十人，陷將士千四百人，宜罪。

translations.literal: The governor-general Shi Pu was ordered to investigate; beheadings and captures amounted to only thirty or forty persons, and one thousand four hundred officers and soldiers had been lost — he deserved punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shi Pu was ordered to investigate and found only thirty or forty actual kills, while 1,400 officers and men had been lost — grounds for punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔令殺賊自效。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to redeem himself by killing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to redeem himself by killing rebels.

sentences.zh: 天順元年隨瑛征天堂諸苗，大獲。

translations.literal: In Tianshun 1 he followed Ying to campaign against the Miao of Tiantang and gained greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun he followed Ying against the Tiantang Miao and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 命充左副總兵，仍鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as left vice commander-in-chief and still garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left vice commander-in-chief and continued to garrison Huguang.

sentences.zh: 已，又偕瑛破蒙能余黨。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again together with Ying broke the remnant followers of Meng Neng.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Ying again in defeating the remnants of Meng Neng's forces.

sentences.zh: 召封武平伯，予世券。

translations.literal: He was recalled and ennobled as Earl of Wuping and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, ennobled as Earl of Wuping, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 孛來犯邊，充遊擊將軍，從安遠侯柳溥等往禦。

translations.literal: When Bolai invaded the border he served as mobile commander and followed the Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Pu, and others to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: When Bolai raided the frontier he served as mobile commander and joined the Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu and others in repelling the invasion.

sentences.zh: 率都指揮趙瑛等與戰，敵敗遁。

translations.literal: Leading the commander-in-chief Zhao Ying and others he joined battle; the enemy was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Leading Commander-in-Chief Zhao Ying and others into battle, he routed the enemy and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 再犯鎮番，復擊卻之，俘百六十人。

translations.literal: When they again invaded Zhenfan he again struck and repelled them and captured one hundred and sixty persons.
translations.idiomatic: When they raided Zhenfan again he repulsed them once more and took 160 captives.

sentences.zh: 尋佩將軍印，充總兵官，討寧夏寇。

translations.literal: Soon bearing the general's seal he served as commander-in-chief to campaign against the raiders of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the general's seal and served as commander-in-chief against the Ningxia raiders.

sentences.zh: 先是，寇大入甘、涼，溥及總兵衛穎等不能禦，惟友稍獲。

translations.literal: Earlier the raiders had made a great incursion into Gan and Liang; Pu and the commander-in-chief Wei Ying and others could not repel them — only You gained a little.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the raiders had swept deep into Gan and Liang; Liu Pu, Commander-in-Chief Wei Ying, and others had failed to stop them, and only You had won any success.

sentences.zh: 至是巡撫芮釗列諸將失事狀，兵部請免友罪。

translations.literal: At this time the grand coordinator Rui Zhao listed the generals' failures in duty; the Ministry of War requested that You's offense be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Rui Zhao then submitted a report on the generals' failures, and the Ministry of War asked that You's punishment be waived.

sentences.zh: 詔並宥溥等。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Pu and the others together.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Liu Pu and the others as well.

sentences.zh: 召還，進侯，卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled, promoted to marquess, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, promoted to marquess, and died.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫綱，弘治中，請友贈謚。

translations.literal: The title passed through his son to his grandson Gang; in the Hongzhi era he requested a posthumous title for You.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down to his grandson Gang, who in the Hongzhi reign requested a posthumous honor for You.

sentences.zh: 詔贈沔國公，謚武僖。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously ennobled him as Duke of Mian with the posthumous title Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously ennobled him as Duke of Mian with the posthumous title Wuxi, "Martial and Delightful."

sentences.zh: 綱傳子勛及熹。

translations.literal: Gang transmitted the title to his sons Xun and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gang passed the title to his sons Xun and Xi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，吏部以友征苗功多冒濫，請停襲。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era the Ministry of Personnel, because You's achievements in campaigning against the Miao were largely inflated, requested that succession be halted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign the Ministry of Personnel, citing the inflated claims in You's Miao campaigns, asked that the line cease to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 熹子大策復得嗣，至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: Xi's son Dace again obtained succession; the line continued until the Ming perished and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Dace inherited the title again, and the line continued until the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 李震，南陽人。

translations.literal: Li Zhen was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父謙，都督僉事，震襲指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Qian was assistant commissioner-in-chief; Zhen inherited the office of commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian had been assistant commissioner-in-chief; Zhen inherited the rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 正統九年從征兀良哈有功，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 9 he followed a campaign against the Urianghai with merit and was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he joined the campaign against the Urianghai with distinction and was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 已，從王驥平麓川，進同知。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed Wang Ji in pacifying Lucchuan and was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Wang Ji in pacifying Lucchuan and was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，充貴州右參將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing came to the throne he served as right deputy general of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi emperor acceded, he served as right deputy general of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 擊苗於偏橋，敗之。

translations.literal: He attacked the Miao at Pianqiao and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Miao at Pianqiao.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年從王來征韋同烈。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 2 he followed Wang Lai to campaign against Wei Tonglie.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he joined Wang Lai in campaigning against Wei Tonglie.

sentences.zh: 破鎖兒、流源諸寨，俘斬千六百人，共克香爐山，獲同烈。

translations.literal: He broke the stockades of Suo'er, Liuyuan, and others, captured and beheaded one thousand six hundred persons, jointly captured Xianglu Mountain, and seized Tonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He took the stockades at Suo'er, Liuyuan, and elsewhere, killing or capturing 1,600 men, then helped capture Xianglu Mountain and seize Wei Tonglie.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使，守靖州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander-in-chief and guarded Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commander-in-chief, he was posted to defend Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋坐罪征還。

translations.literal: Soon for an offense he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital to face charges.

sentences.zh: 方瑛討苗，乞震隨軍，詔許立功贖。

translations.literal: When Fang Ying campaigned against the Miao he requested that Zhen follow the army; an edict permitted him to redeem himself through merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Ying campaigned against the Miao, Zhen asked to join the army, and an edict allowed him to redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 已，從瑛大破天堂諸苗，仍充左參將。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed Ying in utterly defeating the Miao of Tiantang and again served as left deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Ying in a major victory over the Tiantang Miao and was reappointed left deputy general.

sentences.zh: 瑛平銅鼓諸賊，震亦進武岡，克牛欄等五十四寨。

translations.literal: When Ying pacified the bandits of Tonggu and others, Zhen also advanced on Wugang and captured fifty-four stockades including Niulan and others.
translations.idiomatic: While Ying pacified the Tonggu rebels, Zhen advanced into Wugang and took 54 stockades, including Niulan.

sentences.zh: 斬獲多，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Beheadings and captures were many; he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his many kills and captures he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天順中，復從瑛平貴東苗幹把豬。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun era he again followed Ying in pacifying the eastern Guizhou Miao Ganbazhu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign he again followed Ying in suppressing the eastern Guizhou Miao leader Ganbazhu.

sentences.zh: 瑛卒，即以震充總兵官，代鎮貴州、湖廣。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Zhen was immediately appointed commander-in-chief to replace him in garrisoning Guizhou and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Zhen was appointed commander-in-chief in his place to garrison Guizhou and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 初，麻城人李添保以逋賦逃入苗中。

translations.literal: Earlier a man of Macheng, Li Tianbao, fled into the Miao because of tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Tianbao of Macheng had fled among the Miao to escape tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 偽稱唐太宗後，眾萬余，僭王，建元「武烈」，剽掠遠近。

translations.literal: He falsely claimed to be a descendant of Emperor Taizong of Tang, gathered more than ten thousand followers, usurped the title of king, established the era name "Wulie," and plundered near and far.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed descent from Emperor Taizong of Tang, gathered more than ten thousand followers, proclaimed himself king under the era name "Wulie," and raided far and wide.

sentences.zh: 震進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhen advanced to attack and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen advanced against him and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 添保遁入貴州鬼池諸苗中，復誘群苗出掠。

translations.literal: Tianbao fled into the Miao of Guichi's region in Guizhou and again incited the Miao bands to come out and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao escaped into the Guichi Miao of Guizhou and again incited the tribes to raid.

sentences.zh: 震擒之，送京師。

translations.literal: Zhen captured him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen captured him and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋破西堡苗。

translations.literal: Soon he broke the Miao of Xibao.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the Xibao Miao as well.

sentences.zh: 五年春剿城步瑤、僮，攻橫水、城溪、莫宜、中平諸寨，皆破之。

translations.literal: In the spring of year 5 he suppressed the Yao and Zhuang of Chengbu, attacked the stockades of Hengshui, Chengxi, Moyi, Zhongping, and others, and all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he suppressed the Yao and Zhuang of Chengbu, attacking the stockades at Hengshui, Chengxi, Moyi, Zhongping, and elsewhere, and broke them all.

sentences.zh: 長驅至廣西西延，會總兵官過興軍，克十八團諸瑤，前後俘斬數千人。

translations.literal: Driving deep he reached Xiyan in Guangxi, joined the army of the commander-in-chief Guo Xing, captured the various Yao of the Eighteen Tuan, and before and after captured or beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed deep into Xiyan in Guangxi, joined forces with Commander-in-Chief Guo Xing, defeated the Yao of the Eighteen Tuan, and in all killed or captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 其冬命震專鎮湖廣，以李安充總兵，守貴州。

translations.literal: That winter Zhen was ordered to garrison Huguang exclusively, and Li An was appointed commander-in-chief to guard Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhen was ordered to concentrate on garrisoning Huguang, while Li An was appointed commander-in-chief to hold Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年夏率師由錦田、江華抵雲川、桂嶺、橫江諸寨，破瑤，俘斬二千八百余人。

translations.literal: The next summer he led troops from Jintian and Jianghua to the stockades of Yunchuan, Guiling, Hengjiang, and others, broke the Yao, and captured or beheaded more than two thousand eight hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he led his army from Jintian and Jianghua against the stockades at Yunchuan, Guiling, Hengjiang, and elsewhere, defeating the Yao and killing or capturing more than 2,800.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，苗據赤溪湳洞長官司。

translations.literal: In the winter of year 7 the Miao occupied the native office of Chixi Nantong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year the Miao seized the native office of Chixi Nantong.

sentences.zh: 震與安分道進，斬賊渠飛天侯等，破寨二百，遂復長官司。

translations.literal: Zhen and An advanced along separate routes, beheaded the bandit chiefs including Feitian Hou and others, broke two hundred stockades, and thereby restored the native office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Li An advanced on separate routes, killed the rebel leaders including Feitian Hou, took 200 stockades, and restored the native office.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，廣西瑤侵湖南，夜入桂陽州大掠。

translations.literal: The next winter the Yao of Guangxi invaded Hunan, entered Guiyang Prefecture by night, and plundered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Guangxi Yao raided into Hunan, entering Guiyang Prefecture by night and looting on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 震遣兵分道追擊，連敗之，俘斬千余人。

translations.literal: Zhen dispatched troops to pursue along separate routes, repeatedly defeated them, and captured or beheaded more than one thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent troops in pursuit along several routes, routed them in successive engagements, and killed or captured more than 1,000.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，守備靖州。

translations.literal: When the Chenghua era began he defended Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua reign began he was posted to defend Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 都指揮同知莊榮奏貴州黎平諸府密邇湖廣五開諸衛，非大將總領不可，乃復命震兼鎮貴州。

translations.literal: The vice commander-in-chief Zhuang Rong memorialized that the prefectures of Liping in Guizhou and others were close to the guards of Wukai in Huguang and others; without a great general to command overall it would not do, and so Zhen was again ordered to garrison Guizhou concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander-in-Chief Zhuang Rong memorialized that Liping and other Guizhou prefectures lay too close to the Wukai guards of Huguang to be left without a senior commander, and Zhen was again ordered to garrison Guizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，獲賊首苗蟲蝦。

translations.literal: Before long he captured the bandit chief Miao Chongxia.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he captured the rebel leader Miao Chongxia.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄賊劉千斤、石和尚為亂，震進討。

translations.literal: The bandits Liu Qianjin and Shi Heshang of Jing and Xiang made rebellion; Zhen advanced to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels Liu Qianjin and Shi Heshang rose in Jing and Xiang, Zhen marched against them.

sentences.zh: 賊屢敗，乘勝追及於梅溪賊巢。

translations.literal: The bandits were repeatedly defeated; riding victory he pursued and caught up with them at the bandit nest of Meixi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suffered repeated defeats, and pressing his advantage he pursued them to their stronghold at Meixi.

sentences.zh: 官軍不利，都指揮以下死者三十八人，有詔切責。

translations.literal: The government army fared badly; from commander-in-chief downward thirty-eight died, and there was an edict sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops fared badly, and thirty-eight officers of commander rank and below were killed; an edict sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 白圭等大軍至，震自南漳進兵合擊，大破之，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Bai Gui and the others' great army arrived; Zhen advanced troops from Nanzhang to join the attack, utterly defeated them, and the bandits were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Gui's main army arrived, Zhen marched from Nanzhang to join the combined assault, routed the rebels completely, and the uprising was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都督。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit, he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時武岡、沅靖、銅鼓、五開苗復蜂起，而貴州亦告警。

translations.literal: At that time the Miao of Wugang, Yuanjing, Tonggu, and Wukai again rose like swarming bees, and Guizhou also raised alarms.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Miao uprisings erupted again at Wugang, Yuanjing, Tonggu, and Wukai, and alarms were raised in Guizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 震言貴州終難遙制，請專鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: Zhen said Guizhou ultimately could not be controlled from afar, and requested to garrison Huguang exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen argued that Guizhou could not effectively be commanded from a distance and asked to concentrate his garrison in Huguang alone.

sentences.zh: 許之，乃還兵。

translations.literal: This was granted, and he thereupon returned his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 由銅鼓、天柱分四道進，連破賊，直抵清水江。

translations.literal: Advancing from Tonggu and Tianzhu along four routes, he repeatedly defeated the bandits and pressed straight to the Qingshui River.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from Tonggu and Tianzhu in four columns, defeating the rebels in succession and pushing all the way to the Qingshui River.

sentences.zh: 因苗為導，深入賊境。

translations.literal: Using Miao as guides, he penetrated deep into bandit territory.
translations.idiomatic: With Miao guides he pushed deep into rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 兩月間破巢八百，焚廬舍萬三千，斬獲三千三百。

translations.literal: Within two months he broke eight hundred nests, burned thirteen thousand huts, and beheaded or captured three thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months he destroyed 800 strongholds, burned 13,000 dwellings, and killed or captured 3,300.

sentences.zh: 而廣西瑤劫桂陽者，亦擊斬三千八百有奇。

translations.literal: As for the Yao of Guangxi who had raided Guiyang, he also struck and beheaded more than three thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed more than 3,800 of the Guangxi Yao who had raided Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 當是時，震威名著西南，苗、僚聞風畏懾，呼為「金牌李」。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen's reputation was famed in the southwest; Miao and Liao, hearing of his name, were awed and fearful, and called him "Gold-medal Li."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhen's fame spread throughout the southwest; Miao and Liao peoples feared him at the mere mention of his name and called him "Gold-Medal Li."

sentences.zh: 七年，與項忠討平流賊李原，招撫流民九十萬人，荊、襄遂定。

translations.literal: In year 7, together with Xiang Zhong he campaigned against and pacified the roving bandits under Li Yuan, mollified and settled nine hundred thousand displaced people, and Jing and Xiang were thereby stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Xiang Zhong in suppressing the itinerant rebels led by Li Yuan, resettled 900,000 displaced people, and Jing and Xiang were finally secured.

sentences.zh: 語具忠傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in Zhong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Xiang Zhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 十一年，苗復犯武岡、靖州，湖湘大擾。

translations.literal: In year 11, the Miao again invaded Wugang and Jingzhou, and Huguang and Hunan were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Miao again attacked Wugang and Jingzhou, throwing Huguang and Hunan into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 震與巡撫劉敷等分五道進，破六百二十余寨，俘斬八千五百余人，獲賊孥萬計。

translations.literal: Zhen and the grand coordinator Liu Fu and others advanced along five routes, broke more than six hundred twenty stockades, captured or beheaded more than eight thousand five hundred persons, and seized bandit women and children numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Grand Coordinator Liu Fu divided their forces into five columns, took more than 620 stockades, killed or captured over 8,500 rebels, and seized bandits' families by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 論功封興寧伯。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingning.

sentences.zh: 時武靖侯趙輔、寧晉伯劉聚皆以功封，論者多訾議之，獨震功最高，人無異言。

translations.literal: At that time Marquis of Wujing Zhao Fu and Earl of Ningjin Liu Ju were both enfeoffed for merit; many commentators criticized this, but only Zhen's merit was highest and no one voiced dissent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Marquis of Wujing Zhao Fu and Earl of Ningjin Liu Ju had also received enfeoffments for their campaigns, which many critics questioned — but Zhen's achievements stood above the rest, and no one disputed his reward.

sentences.zh: 參將吳經者，與震有隙。

translations.literal: The deputy general Wu Jing had a rift with Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy general named Wu Jing bore a grudge against Zhen.

sentences.zh: 弟千戶綬為汪直腹心，經屬綬譖之。

translations.literal: His younger brother, company commander Shou, was a trusted confidant of Wang Zhi; Jing had Shou slander Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shou, a company commander, was one of Wang Zhi's inner circle; Wu Jing had Shou denounce Zhen.

sentences.zh: 會直方傾項忠，詞連震，遂逮下獄。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhi was then bringing down Xiang Zhong; the case implicated Zhen, and he was thereupon arrested and thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was at that time plotting against Xiang Zhong, and Zhen was implicated in the case and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 奪爵，降左都督，南京閑住。

translations.literal: His peerage was stripped; he was demoted to left commissioner-in-chief and lived in idleness at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his title, he was reduced to left commissioner-in-chief and given idle residence in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，直遣校尉緝事，言震陰結守備太監覃包，私通貨賂。

translations.literal: Before long Zhi dispatched investigating guards who reported that Zhen had secretly joined with the defense eunuch Tan Bao and exchanged bribes in private.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Zhi sent guards to investigate, reporting that Zhen had secretly colluded with the defense eunuch Tan Bao and exchanged bribes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣直赴南京數包等罪，責降包孝陵司香，勒震回京。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, sent Zhi to Nanjing to enumerate the crimes of Bao and others, demoted Bao to burn incense at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and ordered Zhen back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. He sent Wang Zhi to Nanjing to enumerate Tan Bao's crimes, demoted Bao to tend incense at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and ordered Zhen to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 直敗，震訴復爵，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Zhi fell, Zhen appealed and recovered his peerage; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi fell from power, Zhen petitioned and regained his title, but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 震在湖湘久，熟知苗情，善用兵。

translations.literal: Zhen had long been in Huguang and Hunan, thoroughly understood Miao conditions, and was skilled in deploying troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had long served in Huguang and Hunan, knew the Miao well, and was a skilled commander.

sentences.zh: 一時征苗功，方瑛後震為最。

translations.literal: Among the achievements of campaigning against the Miao in that age, after Fang Ying, Zhen's were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Of all those who campaigned against the Miao in that era, only Fang Ying surpassed Zhen in achievement.

sentences.zh: 然貪功好進，事交結，竟以是敗。

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy for merit and eager to advance, engaged in factional dealings, and in the end failed because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was ambitious for credit and advancement, cultivated political connections, and in the end was ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 王信，字君實，南鄭人。

translations.literal: Wang Xin, style Junshi, was a man of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin, courtesy name Junshi, was from Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 生半歲，父忠征北戰歿，母嶽氏苦節育之，後俱獲旌。

translations.literal: When he was half a year old his father Zhong died in battle on the northern campaign; his mother, née Yue, raised him in chaste hardship, and both later received commendations.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six months old his father Zhong was killed on the northern campaign; his mother, Lady Yue, raised him in widowhood and chaste hardship, and both were later honored with imperial commendations.

sentences.zh: 正統中，信襲寬河衛千戶。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era Xin inherited the post of company commander in Kuanhe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign Xin inherited a company command in Kuanhe Guard.

sentences.zh: 成化初，積功至都指揮僉事，守備荊、襄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, accumulating merit he rose to assistant commander, defending Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign he rose through merit to assistant commander and was posted to defend Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 劉千斤反，信以房縣險，進據之。

translations.literal: Liu Qianjin rebelled; Xin, because Fang County was strategically perilous, advanced and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qianjin rebelled, Xin seized Fang County, whose terrain made it a vital strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 民兵不滿千人，賊眾四千突至，圍其城。

translations.literal: The militia numbered fewer than one thousand; four thousand bandits suddenly arrived and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer than 1,000 militiamen, he faced a sudden assault by 4,000 rebels who besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 拒四十余日，選死士，出城五六里舉炮。

translations.literal: He resisted for more than forty days, selected dare-to-die warriors, went out of the city five or six li, and fired cannon.
translations.idiomatic: He held out for more than forty days, then selected elite warriors, sallied five or six li beyond the walls, and fired his cannon.

sentences.zh: 賊疑援至，驚走，追敗之。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected reinforcements had arrived, fled in alarm, and he pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected reinforcements had arrived, broke and fled in panic, and he pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 已，白圭統大軍至，以信為右參將，分道抵後巖山，賊遂滅。

translations.literal: Thereafter Bai Gui arrived leading the great army; Xin was made right deputy general, they reached Houshayan by separate routes, and the bandits were thereby destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bai Gui arrived with the main army; Xin was appointed right deputy general, and their columns converged on Houshayan, destroying the rebels.

sentences.zh: 論功，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 賊黨石龍復陷巫山，信與諸將共平之。

translations.literal: The bandit partisan Shi Long again seized Wushan; Xin together with the various generals jointly pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Shi Long seized Wushan again; Xin and the other commanders together recovered it.

sentences.zh: 而流民仍嘯荊、襄、南陽間。

translations.literal: Yet displaced people still roved and cried out between Jing, Xiang, and Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet displaced communities still roved and raided across Jing, Xiang, and Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 信以為憂，言於朝，即命信兼督南陽軍務。

translations.literal: Xin regarded this with worry and spoke of it at court; he was immediately ordered to concurrently supervise Nanyang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply concerned, Xin reported this to the court and was immediately appointed to oversee Nanyang military affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 賊首李原等果亂，信復與項忠討平之。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Li Yuan and others indeed made rebellion; Xin again together with Xiang Zhong campaigned against and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders Li Yuan and others rose as he had feared; Xin again joined Xiang Zhong in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 擢署都督僉事，鎮守臨清。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and garrisoned Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and posted to garrison Linqing.

sentences.zh: 十三年以本官佩平蠻將軍印，移鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: In year 13, with his existing rank he was invested with the seal of General Who Pacifies the Man and transferred to garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he retained his existing rank while receiving the seal of General Who Pacifies the Man and was transferred to garrison Huguang.

sentences.zh: 永順、保靖二宣慰世相仇殺，信諭以禍福，兵即解。

translations.literal: The two pacification commissioners of Yongshun and Baojing had for generations mutually hated and killed; Xin admonished them with talk of fortune and disaster, and their armies immediately dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongshun and Baojing pacification commissioners had feuded for generations; Xin lectured them on the consequences of their conflict, and their armies stood down at once.

sentences.zh: 靖州及武岡蠻久不戢，守臣議剿之。

translations.literal: The Man of Jingzhou and Wugang had long been unrestrained; defending officials debated exterminating them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Jingzhou and Wugang had long been unruly, and local officials debated a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 信親詣，犒以牛酒，責其無狀，眾稽顙服罪。

translations.literal: Xin went in person, rewarded them with oxen and wine, reproached their misconduct, and the multitude kowtowed and submitted to guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xin went in person, regaled them with feasts of oxen and wine, reproached their misconduct, and the tribes kowtowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 十七年疏言：「湖廣諸蠻雖腹心蠹，實無能為。

translations.literal: In year 17 he memorialized saying: "The various Man of Huguang, though they are a pest within our vitals, in fact cannot accomplish anything.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized: "The tribal peoples of Huguang are a chronic internal affliction, but in truth they can accomplish little on their own.

sentences.zh: 久不靖者，由我將士利其竊發以邀功也。

translations.literal: Those long not pacified are because our officers and soldiers profit from their secret eruptions to seek merit.
translations.idiomatic: The reason unrest persists is that our officers and soldiers profit whenever outbreaks occur and use them to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 選精銳，慎堤防，其患自息。

translations.literal: Select elite troops, carefully maintain defenses, and their trouble will cease of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If we select elite troops and maintain our defenses carefully, the trouble will subside on its own.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄流逋，本避徭役，濫誅恐傷天和。

translations.literal: The displaced fugitives of Jing and Xiang originally fled to avoid corvée labor; indiscriminate execution would fear harming Heaven's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced fugitives of Jing and Xiang fled chiefly to escape corvée labor; indiscriminate killings would threaten the moral order.

sentences.zh: 南畝之氓鹹無蓄積。

translations.literal: The common folk of the southern fields all have no accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: The peasants in the fields have nothing set aside in store.

sentences.zh: 收獲未竟，餱糧已空；

translations.literal: The harvest is not yet finished, yet their travel rations are already empty;
translations.idiomatic: Before the harvest is even finished, their grain for travel is gone;

sentences.zh: 機杼方停，布縷何在。

translations.literal: The loom has just stopped, where are cloth and thread?
translations.idiomatic: The loom has only just fallen silent — where is there cloth to be had?

sentences.zh: 乞選公正仁惠守令，加意撫綏。

translations.literal: I beg to select upright, benevolent, and kind prefects and magistrates and give special attention to mollification.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that upright and benevolent local officials be selected and given special charge to pacify and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 濫授冗員，無慮千百，無一矢勞，冒崇階之賞，乞察勘削奪。」

translations.literal: Superfluous appointees carelessly granted number no less than a thousand or hundreds; with not one arrow's labor they seize rewards of exalted rank — I beg to investigate and strip them."
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds upon hundreds of superfluous appointments have been handed out — men who have never seen battle yet claim rewards of the highest rank. I ask that these be investigated and revoked."

sentences.zh: 部指揮劉斌、張全智勇，力薦於朝。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders Liu Bin and Zhang Quan were wise and brave and vigorously recommended them at court.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commanders Liu Bin and Zhang Quan, men of courage and wisdom, strongly endorsed his recommendations at court.

sentences.zh: 且云：「英雄之士，處心剛正，安肯俯首求媚。

translations.literal: And they said: "Men of heroic quality, whose hearts dwell in upright firmness, how would they willingly bow their heads to seek favor?
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Heroic men of upright character would never stoop to flattery.

sentences.zh: 若不加意延訪，則誌士沈淪，朝廷安得而用之。」

translations.literal: If one does not deliberately seek them out and invite them, then men of resolute purpose sink into obscurity — how can the court obtain and employ them?"
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not actively seek them out, worthy men will languish in obscurity — and how will the throne ever find servants to employ?"

sentences.zh: 二十一年，巡撫馬馴等言，副總兵周賢、參將彭倫官皆都督僉事，而信反止署職，宜量進一秩以重其權。

translations.literal: In year 21, the grand coordinator Ma Xun and others said that the deputy commander-in-chief Zhou Xian and the deputy general Peng Lun were both assistant commissioners-in-chief, whereas Xin on the contrary held only an acting appointment — one rank should be advanced by measure to strengthen his authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Grand Coordinator Ma Xun and others noted that Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhou Xian and Deputy General Peng Lun held the rank of assistant commissioner-in-chief, while Xin remained only in acting appointment — they argued his rank should be raised one step to strengthen his authority.

sentences.zh: 兵部言信無軍功。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said Xin had no military merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War objected that Xin had no recent military achievements.

sentences.zh: 帝特擢為都督同知。

translations.literal: The emperor specially promoted him to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled them and promoted him to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 頃之，改總督漕運。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to grand coordinator of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to oversee the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 帥府舊有湖，擅為利，信開以泊漕艘。

translations.literal: The commandery headquarters had an old lake that was monopolized for private profit; Xin opened it for grain-transport ships to moor.
translations.idiomatic: The regional command had kept an old lake closed for private profit; Xin opened it for grain-transport vessels to moor.

sentences.zh: 勢要壅水，一裁以法，漕務修舉。

translations.literal: Powerful persons dammed the water; he cut them down with the law in one stroke, and grain transport affairs were restored and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful interests had obstructed the waterways; he enforced the law without favor, and the transport service was restored to good order.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 信沈毅簡重，好觀書，被服儒雅。

translations.literal: Xin was deep, resolute, simple, and weighty; he loved reading books, and his dress was refined and scholarly.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was grave, steadfast, and dignified; he loved books and dressed with the bearing of a scholar.

sentences.zh: 歷大鎮，不營私產。

translations.literal: Serving in great garrisons, he did not manage private property.
translations.idiomatic: Though he commanded major garrisons, he never built up private wealth.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「儉足以久，死後不累子孫，所遺多矣。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Frugality suffices to endure; after death not burdening one's sons and grandsons — in that what one bequeaths is already much."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Frugality is enough to last a lifetime; if I do not burden my descendants after death, that alone is a rich legacy."

sentences.zh: 故人婚喪，傾資助之。

translations.literal: When old friends had weddings or funerals, he poured out his resources to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: When old friends faced weddings or funerals, he gave freely of whatever he had.

sentences.zh: 子繼善、從善皆舉進士。

translations.literal: His sons Jishan and Congshan both passed the metropolitan examinations as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jishan and Congshan both earned their jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 繼信總漕運者，寧津都勝、合肥郭鋐。

translations.literal: Those who succeeded Xin as overall coordinators of grain transport were Du Sheng of Ningjin and Guo Tong of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Those who succeeded Xin as grand coordinators of grain transport were Du Sheng of Ningjin and Guo Tong of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 勝襲職南京羽林左衛指揮僉事，鋐襲彭城衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Sheng inherited the post of assistant commander of the Left Yulin Guard at Nanjing; Tong inherited the post of commander of Pengcheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng inherited a post as assistant commander in the Left Yulin Guard at Nanjing; Tong inherited command of Pengcheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 成化初，勝擢署都指揮僉事，而鋐亦以從征荔浦功，進都指揮僉事，中武舉，遷同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua Sheng was promoted to acting assistant commander, while Tong also for merit in following the campaign at Lipu was promoted to assistant commander, passed the military examinations, and was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign Sheng rose to acting assistant commander; Tong earned the same rank for service in the Lipu campaign, passed the military examinations, and was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 勝備倭揚州，擊敗鹽徒為亂者。

translations.literal: Sheng defended against Japanese pirates at Yangzhou and struck down the salt-gangs who made rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng defended Yangzhou against piracy and defeated the salt smugglers who had risen in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尹旻等舉勝將才，鋐亦為張懋所舉。

translations.literal: Yin Min and others recommended Sheng's talent as a general; Tong was also recommended by Zhang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Min and others recommended Sheng as a general of talent; Tong was likewise recommended by Zhang Mao.

sentences.zh: 乃命勝充參將，協同漕運，而鋐代之備倭。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sheng was appointed deputy general to assist in grain transport jointly, while Tong replaced him in defense against Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was appointed deputy general to assist with grain transport, while Tong took his place defending against piracy.

sentences.zh: 陜西大饑，勝奉詔輸米百萬石往振。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered great famine; Sheng received an edict to transport one million shi of rice to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi suffered a severe famine, Sheng was ordered to transport one million shi of rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 信卒，遂遷署都指揮使，充總兵官代之，鋐代勝為參將。

translations.literal: When Xin died, Sheng was thereupon transferred to acting commander and appointed commander-in-chief to replace him; Tong replaced Sheng as deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin died, Sheng was promoted to acting commander and appointed commander-in-chief in his place; Tong succeeded Sheng as deputy general.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，勝以都督僉事帶俸南京前府。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era Sheng served as assistant commissioner-in-chief drawing salary at the Nanjing Front Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign Sheng held the rank of assistant commissioner-in-chief with pay at the Nanjing Front Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 時鋐已鎮守廣西副總兵，破府江僮賊，遂以時望擢總漕運。

translations.literal: At that time Tong was already deputy commander-in-chief garrisoning Guangxi; he broke the Zhuang bandits of Fujiang, and thereupon by contemporary esteem was promoted to overall coordinator of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tong was deputy commander-in-chief in Guangxi; after defeating the Zhuang rebels of Fujiang, he was promoted on the strength of his reputation to oversee grain transport.

sentences.zh: 鋐沈毅有將略。

translations.literal: Tong was deep, resolute, and possessed strategy of a general.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was resolute and possessed genuine strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 而勝無汗馬勛，徒以居官廉靜，故頻有任使。

translations.literal: Sheng, however, had no battle-scar merit; he relied solely on holding office with integrity and quietness, and therefore frequently received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, by contrast, had no battlefield achievements to his credit; he was repeatedly appointed solely because of his integrity and unassuming conduct in office.

sentences.zh: 歷任五十七年，所處皆膏腴地，而自奉簡淡，日食止豆腐，時因以為號。

translations.literal: Across fifty-seven years of service the places he occupied were all fertile and rich lands, yet his own provision was simple and plain; his daily food was only tofu, and at the time people therefore took this as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Over fifty-seven years of service he held posts in some of the empire's richest regions, yet lived modestly on little more than tofu each day — a habit for which people nicknamed him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 鋐累進都督同知，凡軍民利病多陳於朝。

translations.literal: Tong was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief; whatever benefited or harmed army and people he largely set forth at court.
translations.idiomatic: Tong rose through repeated promotions to vice commissioner-in-chief, and frequently memorialized the throne on matters affecting soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 嘗浚通州河二十里，置壩，令淺船搬運，歲省白金數萬。

translations.literal: He once dredged the Tongzhou canal for twenty li, set up dams, ordered shallow boats to transfer cargo, and saved tens of thousands in taels of silver each year.
translations.idiomatic: He once dredged twenty li of the Tongzhou canal, built locks, and arranged for shallow-draft boats to transfer cargo — saving tens of thousands of taels of silver annually.

sentences.zh: 當孝宗時，朝政整肅，文武大臣率得人，鋐筦漕十三年不易。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaozong's time court governance was ordered and strict; civil and military great ministers mostly obtained worthy men; Tong managed grain transport for thirteen years without change.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozong the court was well ordered and its ministers capable; Tong managed the transport service for thirteen years without interruption.

sentences.zh: 正德初，始召佐後府，尋卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was first summoned to assist the Rear Military Commission; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was recalled to assist the Rear Military Commission, but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 彭倫，初職為湖廣永定衛指揮使，累功至都指揮同知。

translations.literal: Peng Lun's initial office was commander of Yongding Guard in Huguang; through accumulated merit he rose to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Lun began as commander of Yongding Guard in Huguang and rose through repeated campaigns to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 成化初，從趙輔平大藤峽賊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he followed Zhao Fu in pacifying the bandits of the Great Rattan Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign he joined Zhao Fu in suppressing the rebels of the Great Rattan Gorge.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使，守備貴州清浪諸處，討破茅坪、銅鼓叛苗。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander, defended Qinglang and other places in Guizhou, and campaigned against and broke the rebellious Miao of Maoping and Tonggu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commander, he defended Qinglang and other posts in Guizhou and defeated the rebel Miao of Maoping and Tonggu.

sentences.zh: 賊掠乾溪，倫討之。

translations.literal: The bandits plundered Qianxi; Lun campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels raided Qianxi, Lun marched against them.

sentences.zh: 賊還所掠，與盟而退。

translations.literal: The bandits returned what they had plundered, made alliance, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels returned their plunder, made peace, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 倫以賊入時，道邛水諸寨，不即邀遏，乃下令，賊入境能生致者予重賞，縱者置諸法。

translations.literal: Lun, because when the bandits entered they had passed through the stockades of Qiongshui and others without being immediately intercepted, thereupon issued an order: those who could capture bandits alive when they entered the territory would receive heavy reward; those who let them go would be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Lun noted that the rebels had passed through the Qiongshui stockades without being stopped. He issued an order: anyone who captured invaders alive would receive a heavy reward; anyone who let them pass would face the full penalty of the law.

sentences.zh: 由是諸司各約所屬，凡生苗軼入，即擒之，送帳下者累累。

translations.literal: From this the various offices each bound their subordinates; whenever raw Miao crossed the border unlawfully, they were immediately seized, and those delivered to his headquarters were piled up in number.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every office bound its subordinates to the order: whenever unregistered Miao crossed the border they were seized at once, and captives delivered to Lun's camp came in droves.

sentences.zh: 倫大會所部目、把縛俘囚，置高竿，集健卒亂射殺之，復割裂肢體，烹啖諸壯士。

translations.literal: Lun greatly assembled the junior officers and squad leaders of his command, bound the captives, set them on high poles, gathered stalwart soldiers to shoot them down in disorder and kill them, then again cut apart limbs and bodies and boiled them for the brave warriors to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Lun summoned his officers, bound the prisoners to tall stakes, and had his soldiers shoot them to death. He then dismembered the bodies and had his troops boil and eat the flesh.

sentences.zh: 罪輕者截耳鼻使去，曰：「以此識，再犯不赦矣。」

translations.literal: Those of lighter guilt had ears and nose cut off and were sent away; he said: "Take this as a mark — if you offend again there will be no pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Lesser offenders had their ears and noses cut off and were sent away with the warning: "Remember this mark — repeat offenders will not be spared."

sentences.zh: 因令諸寨樹牌為界，群苗股栗不敢犯。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the various stockades to erect tablets as boundaries; the Miao masses trembled in their thighs and dared not invade.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered boundary markers erected at every stockade, and the Miao tribes trembled with fear and dared not cross.

sentences.zh: 明年充右參將，仍鎮清浪。

translations.literal: The next year he served as right deputy general and still garrisoned Qinglang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed right deputy general and continued to garrison Qinglang.

sentences.zh: 益盡心邊計，戎事畢舉。

translations.literal: He all the more devoted his heart to frontier planning; military affairs were wholly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself ever more wholeheartedly to frontier affairs, and military responsibilities were fully discharged.

sentences.zh: 妖賊石全州潛入絞洞，煽動古州苗，洪江、甘篆諸苗鹹應之。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-bandit Shi Quanzhou secretly entered Jiaodong, incited the Miao of Guzhou, and the Miao of Hongjiang, Ganzhuan, and others all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-rebel Shi Quanzhou slipped into Jiaodong and stirred up the Guzhou Miao; the tribes of Hongjiang, Ganzhuan, and elsewhere rose in response.

sentences.zh: 倫遣兵截擒，並搜獲其妻子。

translations.literal: Lun dispatched troops to intercept and capture him, and also searched out and seized his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent troops to intercept and capture him, along with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 諸苗將攻鎮遠，倫大敗之，斬首及墮崖死者無算。

translations.literal: The various Miao were about to attack Zhenyuan; Lun greatly defeated them; those beheaded and those who fell from cliffs to their deaths were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao tribes were poised to attack Zhenyuan, Lun routed them utterly. The dead—beheaded or hurled from the cliffs—were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 無何，邛水十四寨苗糾洪江生苗為逆。

translations.literal: Before long, the Miao of the fourteen stockades of Qiongshui gathered the raw Miao of Hongjiang in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Miao of Qiongshui's fourteen stockades stirred up the raw Miao of Hongjiang to revolt.

sentences.zh: 倫分五哨往，甫行，雨如註，倫曰：「賊不虞我，急趨之，可得誌也。」

translations.literal: Lun divided five columns and went; just as they set out, rain poured in torrents; Lun said: "The bandits do not expect us — hurry toward them and we can achieve the goal."
translations.idiomatic: Lun divided his force into five columns and set out. Hardly had they marched when rain fell in torrents. Lun said: "The enemy won't expect us in this weather — press on quickly and we can bring them to book."

sentences.zh: 競進夾攻，縶其魁，俘斬余黨。

translations.literal: They vied to advance and attacked from both sides, bound their chieftain, and captured and beheaded the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed forward at once, attacked from both flanks, seized the rebel chief, and captured or executed the rest.

sentences.zh: 賊盡平。

translations.literal: The bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were completely suppressed.

sentences.zh: 靖州苗亂，湖廣總兵官李震檄倫會討。

translations.literal: The Miao of Jingzhou rebelled; the regional military commander of Huguang Li Zhen dispatched orders for Lun to join in the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou Miao rose in revolt, Li Zhen, commander-in-chief of Huguang, summoned Lun to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍至邛水江，諸熟苗驚，欲竄。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Qiongshui River, the various settled Miao were alarmed and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the Qiongshui River, the settled Miao tribes were terrified and about to scatter.

sentences.zh: 倫與僉事李晃計曰「苗竄必助賊」，乃急撫定之。

translations.literal: Lun and Assistant Commissioner Li Huang planned together, saying "If the Miao flee they will surely aid the bandits," and thereupon urgently pacified and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Lun consulted with Assistant Commissioner Li Huang, saying, "If the Miao flee they will only join the rebels." He moved quickly to reassure and settle them.

sentences.zh: 又緣道降天堂、小坪諸苗。

translations.literal: He also along the route received the surrender of the Miao of Tiantang, Xiaoping, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route he also accepted the submission of the Tiantang and Xiaoping Miao and others.

sentences.zh: 既抵靖州，倫將右哨，出賊背布營。

translations.literal: Having arrived at Jingzhou, Lun commanded the right column, came out behind the bandits' backs, and deployed camp.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jingzhou, Lun took the right column, swung behind the rebels, and encamped.

sentences.zh: 賊走據高山，倫軍仰攻之，賊敗走。

translations.literal: The bandits fled and occupied high mountains; Lun's army attacked upward at them; the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated to the high peaks. Lun's troops attacked uphill and drove them from the heights in defeat.

sentences.zh: 遂渡江，搗其巢，大獲。

translations.literal: He thereupon crossed the river, struck their lairs, and gained greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river, raided their strongholds, and took a great haul of booty and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻白崖塘。

translations.literal: Riding the victory, he attacked Baiyatang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage, he attacked Baiyatang.

sentences.zh: 崖高萬仞，下臨深淵，稱絕險。

translations.literal: The cliff was ten thousand ren high; below it looked down on a deep abyss — called absolutely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The cliff rose thousands of feet sheer, overhanging a deep chasm — a place of legendary impregnability.

sentences.zh: 倫會左哨同進，得徑路。

translations.literal: Lun joined with the left column to advance together and obtained a path.
translations.idiomatic: Lun rendezvoused with the left column and together they found a path to the top.

sentences.zh: 夜登，賊倉皇潰。

translations.literal: By night they ascended; the bandits fled in panic and disarray.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled the heights by night and the rebels broke and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 追斬二千余級，俘獲如之，盡夷其寨。

translations.literal: In pursuit they beheaded more than two thousand; captives and booty were in like measure; they utterly razed their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit yielded more than two thousand heads; captives and spoils were equally abundant, and every stockade was razed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 初，臻剖、六洞苗侵熟苗田，不輸賦，又不供驛馬，有司莫敢問。

translations.literal: Initially, the Miao of Zhenpou and Liudong invaded the fields of settled Miao, did not pay taxes, and also did not supply relay horses — the officials dared not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Miao of Zhenpou and the Six Caves had been seizing fields from settled tribes, paying no taxes and refusing to supply relay horses — and no local official dared confront them.

sentences.zh: 倫遣人諭之，頓首請如制。

translations.literal: Lun sent men to instruct them; they bowed their heads and requested to comply with the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent envoys to summon them to account; they kowtowed and promised to obey the law.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Recording merit, he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded and he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 久之，御史鄧庠、員外郎費瑄勘事貴州，總兵官吳經等皆被劾，獨薦倫智謀老成。

translations.literal: After a long time, Censor Deng Ku and Department Director Fei Xuan investigated matters in Guizhou; the regional military commander Wu Jing and others were all impeached, but he alone recommended Lun as wise in counsel and mature in experience.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, when Censor Deng Ku and Department Director Fei Xuan investigated affairs in Guizhou, they impeached Regional Commander Wu Jing and others — but singled out Lun for commendation as shrewd and seasoned.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，經論罷，即以倫代。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Wu Jing was dismissed after impeachment, and Lun was immediately appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign Wu Jing was removed from office, and Lun was appointed in his stead.

sentences.zh: 倫用師，先計後戰，故多功。

translations.literal: When Lun employed troops, he planned first and fought afterward; thus he had many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Lun always planned before he fought, and this is why he won so often.

sentences.zh: 四年以老致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 卒，予恤如制。

translations.literal: He died; condolence allowances were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and the usual posthumous honors were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 歐磐，滁人。

translations.literal: Ou Pan, a man of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ou Pan was a native of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 襲世職指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office of garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited a hereditary post as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 成化中，擢廣東都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign he was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he was promoted to assistant commander of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 屢剿蠻寇有功。

translations.literal: Repeatedly suppressing barbarian bandits, he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He earned repeated distinctions suppressing tribal raiders.

sentences.zh: 用總督朱英薦，充廣西右參將，分守柳州、慶遠。

translations.literal: On Governor-General Zhu Ying's recommendation, he served as right deputy general of Guangxi, separately defending Liuzhou and Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Governor-General Zhu Ying, he was appointed right deputy general of Guangxi with responsibility for Liuzhou and Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 與左參將馬義討融縣八寨瑤，克之。

translations.literal: Together with left deputy general Ma Yi he campaigned against the Yao of the Eight Stockades of Rong County and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Left Deputy General Ma Yi he subdued the Yao of Rong County's Eight Stockades.

sentences.zh: 師旋。

translations.literal: The army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 余賊復出掠，被劾。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits again came out to plunder; he was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining rebels resumed raiding, and he was impeached.

sentences.zh: 帝絀磐等功，但恤死事家。

translations.literal: The Emperor reduced Pan and others' merits to ribbons but only consoled the families of those who died in service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Pan and his colleagues of credit for the campaign but granted relief to the families of the dead.

sentences.zh: 瑤賊方公強亂，兵部劾總鎮中官顧恒，並及磐，當謫戍。

translations.literal: Yao bandit Fang Gongqiang rebelled; the Ministry of War impeached the supervising eunuch Gu Heng and by extension Pan — they should be banished to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao rebel Fang Gongqiang rose in revolt, the Ministry of War impeached the supervising eunuch Gu Heng and implicated Pan as well; both faced banishment to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 督撫奏：「磐所守乃瑤、僮出沒地。

translations.literal: The governor and grand coordinator memorialized: "What Pan guards is territory where Yao and Zhuang appear and disappear.
translations.idiomatic: The governor and grand coordinator reported: "Pan's post lies in territory where Yao and Zhuang raiders come and go.

sentences.zh: 磐募死士，夜入賊巢，斬其渠胡公返，威震群蠻。

translations.literal: Pan recruited death-defying soldiers, entered the bandits' nest by night, beheaded their leader Hu Gong and returned; awe shook all the barbarian tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Pan recruited daredevils, raided the rebel camp by night, beheaded the ringleader Hu Gong, and returned — his reputation awed every tribe in the region.

sentences.zh: 論功，可贖罪。」

translations.literal: Judging merit, his crimes could be redeemed."
translations.idiomatic: Given his service, his penalty could be commuted."

sentences.zh: 帝乃宥之，還故任。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned him and restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him and restored him to his former command.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，郁林陸川賊黃公定、胡公明等亂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, bandits Huang Gongding, Hu Gongming, and others of Yulin and Luchuan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, Huang Gongding, Hu Gongming, and other rebels in Yulin and Luchuan rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 磐偕按察使陶魯等分五道攻破之。

translations.literal: Pan together with Regional Inspector Tao Lu and others divided into five routes and broke through them.
translations.idiomatic: Pan joined Regional Inspector Tao Lu and others in a five-column assault that broke the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，謝病解職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, he resigned his post on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he resigned on grounds of ill health.

sentences.zh: 總督秦纮言磐多歷戰陣，有才有守，乞起用。

translations.literal: Governor-General Qin Hong said Pan had much experience in battle formations, had talent and integrity, and requested his reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Qin Hong reported that Pan was battle-tested, capable, and conscientious, and asked that he be recalled to service.

sentences.zh: 詔還任。

translations.literal: An edict restored him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict recalled him to his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，府江永安諸僮亂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the various Zhuang of Fujiang and Yong'an rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Zhuang of Fujiang, Yong'an, and the surrounding districts rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 總督閔珪調兵六萬，分四哨往討。

translations.literal: Governor-General Min Gui mobilized sixty thousand troops and divided four columns to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Min Gui mobilized sixty thousand troops and sent four columns against them.

sentences.zh: 磐自象州、修仁直搗陸峒，所向摧破。

translations.literal: Pan from Xiangzhou and Xiuren directly struck Ludong; wherever he went he crushed and broke through.
translations.idiomatic: Pan marched from Xiangzhou and Xiuren straight into Ludong, crushing every resistance in his path.

sentences.zh: 已，偕諸軍連破山寨百八十，斬首六千有奇。

translations.literal: Soon after, together with the various armies he continuously broke more than one hundred eighty mountain stockades; beheaded heads exceeded six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Working with the other columns, he went on to capture more than 180 mountain strongholds and take over six thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使，遷廣西副總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander and transferred to be deputy regional commander of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander and appointed deputy regional commander of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 思恩土官岑浚築石城於丹良莊，截江括商利。

translations.literal: The native official Cen Jun of Si'en built a stone fortress at Danliangzhuang, cut off the river, and extorted merchants' profits.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Jun, the native ruler of Si'en, built a stone fort at Danliangzhuang, blockaded the river, and extorted tolls from merchants.

sentences.zh: 帥府令毀之，不聽。

translations.literal: The military headquarters ordered it destroyed; he did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The regional headquarters ordered the fort dismantled, but Cen Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 磐自田州還，督兵將毀城。

translations.literal: Pan returned from Tianzhou, supervised troops, and was about to destroy the fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Pan, returning from Tianzhou, gathered troops to tear down the fort.

sentences.zh: 浚率眾拒，擊敗之，卒夷其城。

translations.literal: Jun led the masses to resist; Pan defeated him and in the end razed the fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Jun mustered his men to resist, but Pan defeated him and razed the fort to the ground.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄧廷瓚等以磐功多，言於朝，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Deng Tingzan and others, because Pan's achievements were many, spoke to the court; he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Deng Tingzan and others, citing Pan's many achievements, memorialized the court, and he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年命佩平蠻將軍印，鎮守湖廣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was granted the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and assigned to garrison Huguang.

sentences.zh: 磐為將廉，能得士。

translations.literal: Pan as general was incorrupt and could win over soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Pan was upright and won the loyalty of his men.

sentences.zh: 久鎮南邦，蠻人畏服。

translations.literal: Long garrisoning the southern realm, the barbarians feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After years on the southern frontier, the tribal peoples feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 十八年請老，又二年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he requested retirement on age; two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he requested retirement; two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 祭葬如制。

translations.literal: Sacrifice and burial according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial and burial honors were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 張祐，字天祐，廣州人。

translations.literal: Zhang You, styled Tianyou, a man of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You, courtesy name Tianyou, was a native of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼好學能文。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and could compose writing.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved learning and had a gift for letters.

sentences.zh: 弘治中襲世職為廣州右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign he inherited the hereditary office as garrison commander of Guangzhou Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he inherited his family's post as commander of Guangzhou Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 年十九，從總督潘蕃征南海寇禢元祖，先登有功。

translations.literal: At nineteen years old, he followed Governor-General Pan Fan to campaign against the maritime bandit Ta Yuanzu of the South Sea; he was first to ascend and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he joined Governor-General Pan Fan's campaign against the South Sea pirate Ta Yuanzu, scaling the walls first and distinguishing himself.

sentences.zh: 正德二年擢署都指揮僉事，守備德慶、瀧水。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was promoted and appointed acting assistant commander-in-chief, defending Deqing and Longshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhengde reign he was appointed acting assistant commander with charge of Deqing and Longshui.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮負險者聞其威信，稍稍遁去。

translations.literal: Yao and Zhuang who relied on perilous terrain heard of his prestige and authority and gradually fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zhuang bandits in the hill country, hearing of his reputation, gradually melted away.

sentences.zh: 總督林廷選引為中軍，事無大小咨焉。

translations.literal: Governor-General Lin Tingxuan brought him in as central army commander; in matters large and small he was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lin Tingxuan made him his chief-of-staff and consulted him on every decision, great or small.

sentences.zh: 守備惠、潮，搗盜魁劉文安、李通寶穴，平之。

translations.literal: Defending Huizhou and Chaozhou, he struck the dens of bandit chiefs Liu Wen'an and Li Tongbao and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: While defending Huizhou and Chaozhou, he raided the lairs of the bandit chiefs Liu Wen'an and Li Tongbao and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西右參將，分守柳、慶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right deputy general of Guangxi, separately defending Liu and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right deputy general of Guangxi with responsibility for Liuzhou and Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 總督陳金討府江賊，命祐進沈沙口，大破之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chen Jin campaigned against Fujiang bandits; he ordered You to advance on Shenshakou and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Chen Jin marched against the Fujiang rebels, he ordered You to advance on Shenshakou and won a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 增俸一等，擢副總兵，鎮守廣西。

translations.literal: His salary was increased one grade; he was promoted to deputy regional commander and garrisoned Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His salary was raised one grade, he was promoted to deputy regional commander, and assigned to garrison Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 尋進署都督僉事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 古田諸瑤、僮亂。

translations.literal: The various Yao and Zhuang of Gutian rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao and Zhuang of Gutian and the surrounding districts rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 祐言：「先年征討，率倚兩江土兵，賞不酬勞。

translations.literal: You said: "In former years when campaigning, we generally relied on native troops of the two rivers; rewards did not repay labor.
translations.idiomatic: You reported: "In past campaigns we relied on native levies from the two river regions, yet their rewards never matched their hardship.

sentences.zh: 今調多失期，乞定議優賚。」

translations.literal: Now when mobilizing, many miss deadlines; I request a settled decision to grant preferential rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Now they often fail to muster on time. I ask that the court set a policy of generous compensation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 督都指揮沈希儀等討臨桂、灌陽諸瑤，斬首五百余級，璽書獎勞。

translations.literal: He supervised Regional Commander Shen Xiyi and others to campaign against the Yao of Lingui, Guanyang, and others; more than five hundred heads were beheaded; an imperial sealed letter rewarded and consoled them.
translations.idiomatic: He directed Regional Commander Shen Xiyi and others against the Yao of Lingui and Guanyang, taking more than five hundred heads; the emperor sent a sealed letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 又連破古田賊，俘斬四千七百，進署都督同知。

translations.literal: Again he continuously broke the Gutian bandits; captives and beheadings numbered four thousand seven hundred; he was advanced to acting vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to crush the Gutian rebels, capturing or killing 4,700, and was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 已，復討平洛容、肇慶、平樂諸蠻。

translations.literal: Soon after, he again campaigned and pacified the barbarians of Luorong, Zhaoqing, Pingle, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the tribes of Luorong, Zhaoqing, Pingle, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 增俸一等，蔭子，世百戶。

translations.literal: His salary was increased one grade; his son received hereditary privilege; a hereditary hundred-household fief.
translations.idiomatic: His salary was raised one grade, and his son received a hereditary hundred-household enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，母喪，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign began, his mother died; grief destroyed him until he was skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign his mother died, and his grief left him emaciated as a skeleton.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾乞休，還衛。

translations.literal: Soon after, on grounds of illness he requested leave and returned to his guard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested retirement on grounds of illness and returned to his home garrison.

sentences.zh: 初，上思州土目黃镠作亂，祐購其黨黃廷寶縛獻之。

translations.literal: Initially, the native officer Huang Liao of Shangsi Prefecture rebelled; You offered a bounty and his follower Huang Tingbao bound and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huang Liao, a native subordinate of Shangsi Prefecture, rebelled, You put a price on his head and Huang Tingbao, one of his own followers, bound him and delivered him up.

sentences.zh: 總督張嵿惡祐不白己，至劾祐懷奸避難，逮系德慶獄。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhang Jun hated that You had not informed him beforehand; he went so far as to impeach You for harboring treachery and avoiding difficulty, and had him arrested and imprisoned in Deqing jail.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhang Jun resented that You had acted without consulting him and impeached him for duplicity and cowardice, having him thrown into prison at Deqing.

sentences.zh: 數上書訟冤，釋令閑住。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials proclaiming innocence; he was released and ordered to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated petitions proclaiming his innocence, he was released and placed on inactive status.

sentences.zh: 盧蘇、王受亂田州。

translations.literal: Lu Su and Wang Shou rebelled in Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su and Wang Shou raised rebellion in Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 總督姚鏌召至軍中，待以賓禮，多所裨贊。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yao Mo summoned him to the army, treated him with guest ritual, and greatly benefited from his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yao Mo summoned him to headquarters, received him as an honored guest, and drew heavily on his counsel.

sentences.zh: 後王守仁代鏌，詢撫剿之宜，祐曰：「以夷治夷，可不煩兵而下。」

translations.literal: Later Wang Yangming replaced Mo; he inquired about the appropriate measures for pacification and suppression; You said: "Use barbarians to govern barbarians — without troubling troops they can be brought down."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yangming succeeded Yao Mo, he asked You's advice on pacification and suppression. You said: "Let the tribes handle the tribes — you can bring them to heel without exhausting your army."

sentences.zh: 守仁納之，蘇、受果效順。

translations.literal: Yangming accepted it; Su and Shou indeed submitted in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Yangming took his advice, and Lu Su and Wang Shou duly submitted.

sentences.zh: 因命祐部分其眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered You to apportion their followers.
translations.idiomatic: He then put You in charge of reorganizing their followers.

sentences.zh: 事寧，守仁言：「思、田初定，宜設一副總兵鎮之，請即以命祐。」

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Yangming said: "Si and Tian have just been pacified; a deputy regional commander should be established to garrison them — I request that You be appointed forthwith."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was settled, Yangming reported: "Si'en and Tianzhou are only newly pacified — they need a deputy regional commander to hold them. I recommend appointing You."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 破封川賊盤古子，又剿廣東會寧劇賊丘區長等，斬首一千二百，勒銘大隆山。

translations.literal: He broke the Fengchuan bandit Panguzi, again suppressed the fierce bandits of Huining in Guangdong, Qiu Quchang, and others; one thousand two hundred heads were beheaded; an inscription was carved on Dalong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Fengchuan rebel Panguzi, then suppressed the notorious Guangdong brigand Qiu Quchang and his gang at Huining, taking twelve hundred heads and carving an inscription on Mount Dalong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，楊春賊趙林花陷高州，總督陶諧檄祐討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Yangchun bandit Zhao Linhua captured Gaozhou; Governor-General Tao Xie dispatched orders for You to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Yangchun rebel Zhao Linhua seized Gaozhou, and Governor-General Tao Xie ordered You to march against him.

sentences.zh: 深入，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: He penetrated deeply; many were beheaded and captured.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed deep into enemy country and took many heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 忽中危疾卒，軍中為哀慟。

translations.literal: Suddenly he was stricken with a grave illness and died; the army mourned him in grief and anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he was stricken with a fatal illness and died; the whole army mourned him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 祐身長八尺，智識絕人。

translations.literal: You's body was eight chi in height; wisdom and knowledge surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: You stood eight feet tall, with intelligence far beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 馭軍有節制，與下同甘苦，不營私產。

translations.literal: In commanding troops he had restraint and discipline; he shared hardship and ease with subordinates and did not pursue private wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with discipline, shared hardship with his men, and never pursued private gain.

sentences.zh: 性好書，每載以自隨，軍暇即延儒生講論。

translations.literal: His nature loved books; each time he carried them with himself; in idle hours in camp he summoned Confucian scholars for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and always traveled with them; whenever military duty slackened he invited scholars to lecture and debate.

sentences.zh: 嘗過烏蠻灘，謁馬伏波祠，太息曰：「歿不俎豆其間，非夫也。」

translations.literal: Once passing Wuman Rapids, he visited the shrine of General Ma Yuan the Wave-Calmer, sighed deeply, and said: "To die without being honored with sacrificial offerings in such a place — that is no true man."
translations.idiomatic: Passing Wuman Rapids one day, he visited the shrine of General Ma Yuan and sighed deeply: "To die without receiving sacrifice in a shrine like this — what kind of man would that be?"

sentences.zh: 題詩而去。

translations.literal: He inscribed a poem and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He left a poem inscribed on the shrine and went his way.

sentences.zh: 後田州人立祠橫山祀之。

translations.literal: Later the people of Tianzhou built a shrine at Hengshan to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the people of Tianzhou erected a shrine on Hengshan to offer him sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：苗蠻阻險自固，易動難服，自其性然。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Miao and tribal peoples hold rugged terrain and fortify themselves; they are quick to stir and hard to pacify — such is their nature.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Miao and other tribal peoples cling to rugged terrain and fortify themselves; they rebel easily and submit with difficulty — such is their nature.

sentences.zh: 而草禽狝，濫殺邀功，貪貨賄，興事端，控馭乖方，綏懷無策，則鎮將之過也。

translations.literal: Yet when commanders hunt them like birds and beasts in the grass, kill recklessly to claim merit, grasp for bribes, provoke incidents, govern by wrong methods, and lack strategies of reassurance and inclusion, the fault lies with the frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: But when frontier commanders treat them like game to be hunted down, slaughter indiscriminately to claim merit, crave bribes, stir up trouble, govern by the wrong methods, and have no policy of reassurance and inclusion — then the fault is the generals' own.

sentences.zh: 韓觀諸人，雖功最焯著，而皆以威信震懾蠻荒。

translations.literal: Han Guan and his like, though their achievements blazed most brightly, all relied on prestige and authority to awe the barbarian wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guan and men of his stamp, for all that their achievements shone brightest, ruled the tribal frontiers through sheer prestige and terror.

sentences.zh: 若山雲、王信、張祐之廉儉有守，士君子何以過？

translations.literal: As for the integrity and restraint of Shan Yun, Wang Xin, and Zhang You — how could even gentlemen surpass them?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Shan Yun, Wang Xin, and Zhang You, who were frugal and principled in office — what gentleman could hope to surpass them?

sentences.zh: 故尤足尚雲。

translations.literal: Therefore Yun is especially worthy of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Shan Yun is especially worthy of admiration.
